d: 'Noid commanders are four-eyed tyhrranoids in Up Your Arsenal. They are the largest and most powerful common tyhrranoid variant, serving as leaders in battle or occupying high-ranking positions. After being converted to robonoids by the Biobliterator in Metropolis, they became known as robonoid commanders.
t: 'Noid commanders are most lethal when ambushing players from elevated positions or when supported by other troops. Their plasma pistols deal serious damage with a rapid fire rate, and their short reload window offers little respite. Their plasma shots also leave temporary residue on surfaces, further restricting movement.

d: 'Noid missile stations are minor enemies in Up Your Arsenal. These tyhrranoid missile launchers are positioned underground to provide anti-aircraft and anti-personnel fire. Ratchet and Clank first encountered them during Operation: ISLAND STRIKE on Kavu Island of Tyhrranosis.

70 millimeter Stalker Turrets are enemies in Deadlocked. They appear in several locations within the Shadow Sector of the Solana Galaxy, first appearing during the Marauder Tournament at the DreadZone Station.

Agorian beasts are enemies in A Crack in Time. Tamed by agorian riders, these bipedal creatures possess powerful hind legs and small, slender forelegs. Their physical characteristics include grayish-purple skin, a toothy jaw, and prominent tusks.

Alien snappers are enemies in Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagined game, with a cameo appearance in Up Your Arsenal. Encountered by Ratchet and Clank primarily within the Blarg Tactical Research Station on Nebula G34, these large creatures possess tough hides and can deliver powerful biting attacks when provoked.

where: Blarg Tactical Research Station, Nebula G34
Blarg Tactical Research Station, Nebula G34

t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002 game)=== In the original release, alien snappers are the most durable medium-sized enemies encountered in the early game. Because they retaliate with a forward bite, the player should avoid close-quarters combat. The OmniWrench is generally ineffective unless thrown using a comet-strike.

d: Alien spawn pods are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are metal objects that spawn both nanophytes and cragpoles.
t: When alien spawn pods appear, they are almost always already accompanied by nanophytes or cragpoles, and will spawn around half a dozen more. The continuous introduction of new enemies via spawn pods can be problematic if left unchecked. The pods on Fastoon are sturdy and not easily defeated, whereas those on Reepor and Igliak succumb very quickly to the much stronger weapons available.

d: Alien spitters are enemies in Ratchet & Clank (2016). Relatives of the alien snappers, they are encountered alongside them by Ratchet and Clank in the Blarg Tactical Research Station on Nebula G34 during the mission "Find the top secret Blarg research project".

where: Blarg Tactical Research Station, Nebula G34

t: Alien spitters are durable enemies that provide lethal long-range support with their acid attacks. While their projectiles follow a predictable arc that is relatively easy to dodge in isolation, they become significantly more dangerous when paired with alien swarmers and snappers.

d: Alien swarmers, also known as crawlers, are recurring enemies in Ratchet & Clank and its 2016 reimagined counterpart. These small, hostile, frog-like blargian experiments are typically encountered within the Blarg Tactical Research Station on Nebula G34 and the Kogor Refinery on Orxon.

where: Blarg Tactical Research Station, Nebula G34
Blarg Tactical Research Station, Nebula G34 Blarg research outpost, Gaspar

t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002)=== In the original release, alien swarmers utilize a zig-zag movement pattern to close the distance to Ratchet before leaping forward to bite. While they are effectively neutralized by area-of-effect weapons like the Pyrocitor or the Suck Cannon, the OmniWrench is often sufficient for dispatching them individually, allowing players to save ammunition for larger threats.

d: Amoeboid kings are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are a colossal version of the large amoeboid, wearing a silver crown encrusted with blue jewels on its tips. Despite their name they have little in common with the king amoeboids who appear in Up Your Arsenal.
Anklebiters are enemies in Ratchet & Clank. They are small, rodent-like predators native to Hoven that inhabit the planet's icy terrain and typically ambush prey in large packs.
t: Due to their durability—requiring two OmniWrench strikes to defeat—and their tendency to attack in groups, anklebiters can be dangerous when they swarm the player. The Walloper is particularly effective, defeating them in a single hit without consuming ammo. Against larger groups, the Pyrocitor offers a safer alternative for keeping them at bay, while the Drone Device provides effective autonomous defense.

d: Anthropods are recurring enemies in the Ratchet & Clank series, appearing in Tools of Destruction, Quest for Booty, A Crack in Time, All 4 One, and Full Frontal Assault.
t: ===Tools of Destruction=== Anthropods are found exclusively at Outpost L51 on Sargasso, appearing alongside grubsnuckers and grunthors. While individually weak and restricted to melee attacks, they serve as a deadly distraction when paired with larger predators. The Tornado Launcher and Shock Ravager are particularly effective at managing their swarms.

d: Anti-virus nanobots are minor enemies in Size Matters. They are small, hovering automatons encountered inside Clank, serving as his internal security system. They have a single eye, red antennae, a jetpack, and a mouth used for biting.

Arc Strikers are enemies in A Crack in Time. They are one of four basic classes of Nefarious Troopers (alongside Splitterbots, Protoguards, and Cyclobombers), fought by Ratchet and Clank across the Breegus System of the Polaris Galaxy.

}} Arctic leviathans are enemies in Going Commando, encountered in the Tundor Wastes on planet Grelbin. They are serpentine creatures with long necks, two large ears akin to the wings of a bat, and large, protruding jaws filled with sharp teeth, with two long and thin growths at the end of their chin.

Argonoids are enemies in Tools of Destruction. Fought exclusively in the Imperial Fight Festival, these "squiggly-armed" sapients are related to paladrones and terraklons. As gladiators, they were either captured or lured to Mukow, where they were forced to fight for the amusement of the Imperial Army's elite troops.
Slorgs are large mollusk-like creatures featured in All 4 One, found throughout the coastal region of Octonok Cay. An enhanced variant, the armored slorg, also appears occasionally.
t: In combat, slorgs function more as environmental hazards than standard enemies. Their electrified bodies damage any player on contact. When shot, they slide uncontrollably at high speeds, often ricocheting off walls, into players, or off ledges. Despite their aquatic appearance, slorgs perish upon hitting water.

d: }} Attack-Copters are enemies in Going Commando that also make brief appearances in Up Your Arsenal. These Thugs-4-Less gunships feature two long wings with underslung cannons.
t: When fighting as Giant Clank, Attack-Copters deal minimal damage and can be destroyed with basic melee attacks. Although they are not a primary concern, players should eliminate them to prevent cumulative damage from large groups, which can become significant toward the end of a boss fight. Upon destruction, they provide ammunition and nanotech.

d: Axebots are enemies in Ratchet & Clank, encountered by Ratchet at the logging site on Eudora during the mission "Explore the mills". These humanoid blargian robots were deployed by Drek Industries for lumberjacking operations, though they utilize their axes to attack intruders.
t: Upon detecting Ratchet, standard axebots charge to close the distance. Once in range, they stop to deliver a horizontal axe swing. Regardless of whether the strike connects, the robot pauses to laugh, leaving it vulnerable to counterattacks. Their animations can be interrupted if they sustain sufficient damage.

d: Backup dancers are minor enemies in Up Your Arsenal, fought only during the mission "Beat Courtney Gears" on Obani Draco. Resembling Courtney Gears, they are purple hotbots with pigtails who serve as her backup dancers. They appear in Gears' music video for "Robots of the Galaxy".

The saboteurs, also known as bandit ships, are enemies in Going Commando, appearing in the Deep Space Disposal Facility, Hrugis Cloud. During "Take out the Saboteurs", twenty saboteurs attacked the facility's sixteen power generators, though Ratchet and Clank destroyed them for a reward in bolts.

}} Saur-beasts are enemies in Going Commando. Barlowian saur-beasts are encountered in the Vukovar Canyon, on Barlow, while Jobian saur-beasts are encountered in the Megacorp Games area, on Joba. They are bipedal reptilian creatures trained by the tribesmen, both the Vukovar and Joba tribesmen respectively.
t: The saur-beasts are very durable, and will either attack by walking to Ratchet and biting, or charging at him when encountering him from a distance and headbutting him. Some tribesmen also ride the saur-beasts, and after they fall off upon sustaining damage, the saur-beasts may then charge.

d: Bash bots are enemies in Up Your Arsenal, encountered during challenges in the Annihilation Nation on Station Q9. They are melee counterparts of the laser bots, and attack with flails attached to their arms.
Battle cruisers are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are large space pirate starships, primarily used to attack and plunder vessels.

Beam Turrets are enemies in Deadlocked. They are fought in Vox Industries' DreadZone gameshow and first appear in Kronos' "Night Flight" and "Dark City Arenas" challenges, and from then on are a recurring enemy in multiple tournaments and battlecourses.

where: DreadZone Station, Kronos, Shaar, Orxon, Torval, Stygia, Maraxus

t: Due to the way the turrets only pop out when close enough, the player is forced to engage them from nearby. When active, they immediately begin charging their laser, which is then discharged shortly after, with the turret slowly sweeping the laser towards any player who attempts to strafe it. It cannot do so very quickly, meaning a player who dodged the initial hit is largely safe.

d: Repair drones are enemies in Going Commando, encountered at the Deep Space Disposal Facility in the Hrugis Cloud. They are purple-colored Megacorp robots used in the facility to repair its defense turrets. They have two arms with yellow pincers pointed forwards, which can repair hover turrets and fire lasers.

Birdbots are robotic enemies featured in the original Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagining. Manufactured by Drek Industries and utilized by the blarg during the invasion of Novalis, these medium-sized combat units are typically encountered in the Tobruk Crater alongside peckbots.
t: ===Overview=== On the ground, birdbots fire their cannons in rapid four-shot bursts. While the original projectiles had limited range, the reimagined version features high-velocity rounds capable of reaching medium-to-long distances. Between volleys, the units remain stationary to reload and recalibrate their aim.

d: Deadlocked: Battledome, DreadZone Station Mining facility, Orxon Torval Maraxus Prison, Maraxus Ghost Station
t: BladeBalls in all games and all versions have the same attack pattern, and the same strategy works against them. They only pose a threat if attacking in a large number, and if they have already reached melee range. In most cases, a simple OmniWrench swing can dispatch them, while a medium-range weapon (in Going Commando, this would be the Lancer or Lava Gun) can be more effective.

d: Blade Minions are collector minions that serve as enemies in All 4 One. First encountered in the Minion Training Center after an alarm is triggered, their design suggests a mechanical connection to the Vac-U's mortar toss technique. Following their introduction, they appear sporadically across planet Magnus.

Blade balls are enemies in Into the Nexus. These small, floating robots serve as the apparent equivalents to Megacorp's PX6 BladeBall and are primarily deployed by the Thugs-4-Less, though the Intergalactic Museum of History also uses them for security.

Blade bots are enemies in Up Your Arsenal encountered within the Annihilation Nation challenges on Station Q9. These small robots feature a single yellow ocular light and a small antenna; they hover toward targets to attack with revolving dual razors.

Bladeballs are enemies appearing in the reimagined Ratchet & Clank. Deployed by Drek Industries to support blargian interests, these small-scale robots typically attack in large swarms. Many are spawned by blarg generators.
t: Individually, bladeballs present a minimal threat due to their low health. However, they are dangerous when swarming or when deployed by mobile blarg generators, which act as high-durability spawners. Focusing exclusively on the bladeballs can leave Ratchet vulnerable to long-range fire from other blarg forces, while ignoring them risks the player being surrounded.

d: The blarg armored transport, also known as the armed transport, Dropship Model X6Z, or colloquially the Dropship of Death, is an enemy vehicle in Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagined game. Manufactured by Drek Industries, these dropships were used to deploy ground troops and provide aerial fire support.
t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002)=== In the original game, these transports are heavily armored and fire homing blasts that explode on impact. Because their projectiles are highly agile, dodging can be difficult. Since these transports usually stay in fixed positions while dropping off commandos, the Visibomb Gun is the most effective way to destroy them from a safe distance.

d: Blarg battleships are enemy vessels in Ratchet & Clank (2016). They are large blargian warships sent by Drek Industries to bomb Fort Krontos on planet Batalia.

Blarg bombthrowers are enemies in Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagined game. While they only appear at Fort Krontos on Batalia in the original title, they are encountered on several more planets in the reimagined version.
t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002)=== In the original game, bombthrowers throw explosives from medium range. These bombs explode on contact or after a short delay; however, the blast radius is small and easily dodged. Because they flee to new cover after every attack, they can be difficult to target.

d: Blarg commanders are enemies in Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagined game. These large, muscular blarg work for Drek Industries and wield heavy pistols in combat. While notably found on planet Kerwan commanding packs of robomutts, their reimagined counterparts also appear in the Blarg Tactical Research Station.

where: Blarg Tactical Research Station, Nebula G34

t: The original commander's pistol fires a single, slow-moving missile with medium-range homing capabilities. If Ratchet approaches, the commander will typically retreat to a new position; however, if the gap is closed quickly, they will perform a melee strike with their pistol. These missiles can be outmaneuvered, shot out of the air, or disintegrated with the Walloper.

d: Blarg destroyers, also known as blarg heavy bombers, are enemies in Ratchet & Clank. They were fought at Fort Krontos on Batalia, during the mission "Destroy the bombers".

Blarg elite commandos, also known as elite guards, are enemies in Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagined game. Serving as Chairman Drek's most formidable troops, they utilize jetpacks and long-range pistols to engage Ratchet and Clank from the air.
t: In the original game, elite commandos are highly dangerous as their flight patterns make them difficult to target. They possess excellent aim and considerable range, firing three-round bursts with their pistols. While individual projectiles are slow enough to dodge, they become overwhelming in large numbers; players should utilize metal crates for cover.

d: Blarg generators are robotic units utilized by Drek Industries in Ratchet & Clank and its 2016 reimagining. These blargian devices function as automated deployment systems for smaller combat robots, including robomutts, scoutbots, chompers, and bladeballs.
t: ===Overview=== The primary function of a generator is to replace destroyed minions with fresh reinforcements. Due to their low health in the original game, generators should be prioritized to prevent endless enemy waves.

d: Blarg gunners are enemies in Ratchet & Clank encountered at the Gemlik Base in Oltanis orbit. These blarg troopers serve Drek Industries by manning specialized defensive emplacements. Ratchet and Clank first encountered them during the mission "Explore base".
t: Once Ratchet enters their line of sight, blarg gunners fire a continuous barrage of bullets. The behavior of the turret varies by its placement: wall-mounted turrets often fire immediately without ceasing, while those in the open may take a split second to lock on before engaging.

d: Blarg heavy interceptors are automated surveillance hovercraft deployed by Drek Industries in Ratchet & Clank.
t: Upon activation, the interceptor summons nearby machinegun turrets to engage the target. Because the interceptors are highly durable and do not attack directly, they are often not worth the ammunition required to destroy them. If engagement is necessary, the Tesla Claw can neutralize them efficiently, while the Drone Device protects against the triggered turrets.

d: The blarg heli-commander is an enemy vehicle in Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagined game. These helicopters are piloted by blarg forces serving Drek Industries and are equipped with mounted machine guns or rocket launchers. They were deployed across several planets, most notably Kerwan, Hoven, and Quartu.
t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002)=== On Kerwan, heli-commanders are dangerous foes that fire rapid-fire machine-gun rounds that are difficult to dodge. They typically maintain a medium distance to avoid counterattacks. While it is possible to sprint past them, it is safer to destroy them with the Blaster from a distance. On Hoven, the units fire four-missile volleys that are easily dodged before the craft repositions.

d: Blarg paratroopers are robotic enemies in Ratchet & Clank. They are infantry units serving the blarg forces, appearing in both standard and elite forms.
t: The primary threat posed by blarg paratroopers is their ability to suppress targets with long-range micro-missile fire. Their constant side-flipping makes them difficult to track with precision weapons. Engaging them from a distance with the Devastator or deploying the Glove of Doom allows for a rapid neutralization before they can establish a firing rhythm.

d: Blarg saucers are enemy fighter-craft piloted by the blarg in Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagined game. These small, agile vessels accompany Drek Industries' planetary invasions and operations in space.
t: Whether controlled via a starship or a ground-based cannon, blarg saucers are easily destroyed by standard machine-gun fire. It is often essential to prioritize them to replenish health or ammunition before focusing on larger targets. Additionally, when saucers focus their fire on the ship, they should be cleared out first to remove the distraction.

d: Blarg space commandos are enemies in Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagined game. These blarg soldiers work for Drek Industries and wear specialized suits to operate in vacuum-exposed or toxic environments, such as the Blarg Tactical Research Station, Gemlik Base, and the uninhabitable planet Orxon.

where: Blarg Tactical Research Station, Nebula G34
Blarg Tactical Research Station, Nebula G34

t: Space commandos fire upon the ground to release a wide stream of energy that travels forward. While this attack is easily dodged by jumping, it can become a hazard if multiple commandos are firing at once. With Ratchet within proximity, they will attempt to whack him with their rifles. The commandos encountered on the Gemlik Base have a slight improvement to their range.

d: Blarg space fighters are enemy vehicles in Ratchet & Clank. These blargian fighter-craft were developed by Drek Industries and encountered by Ratchet and Clank at the Gemlik Base in Oltanis orbit.
t: When encountered on foot at the Gemlik Base, blarg space fighters are formidable due to the high speed and long range of their rockets. The most effective strategy is to remain out of their detection range and utilize the Visibomb Gun to destroy them from a safe distance. If the Visibomb Gun is unavailable, players can use the Decoy Glove to draw their fire, providing an opening to strike back with the Devastator.

d: Blarg troopers are enemies in Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagined game. They are common blargian troops that worked for Chairman Drek and were encountered by Ratchet and Clank on various planets in the Solana Galaxy.
t: On planet Eudora, blarg troopers fire slow-moving energy blasts in three-round bursts. These attacks are easily dodged; after completing a burst, the trooper remains stationary for a moment before resuming fire. If Ratchet enters melee range, they will perform a kick, but if he is just outside of it, they will retreat to maintain firing distance. They are best defeated with the Bomb Glove, Blaster, or Glove of Doom.

d: Bolt thieves are enemies in Ratchet & Clank. They are small, floating, fast robots with two arms, encountered on Batalia, Oltanis, and Kalebo III. Three are hidden throughout Batalia in a small area and will flee if Ratchet approaches, and can be shot for a large sum of bolts.
Bolt thieves: Gordan-Gex, Randolph Dk, Mortimer Dk, Tony-Strk, Coleman, Winthorpe, Billy-Ray, Scrooge McDee
t: Sludge slingers and bolt thieves attacked by continuously firing from their cannons, though sludge slingers fired goo while bolt thieves used supersonic bolts; these bolts can be collected after they have fired if they miss Clank. Both types of robot were easily defeated using stealth takedowns when they turned their backs.

d: Bomb-o-matics are static defensive installments in Ratchet & Clank, encountered within Qwark's headquarters on Umbris during the mission "Survive Qwark's gauntlet". These automated sentries rapidly fire cannonballs in a circular radius to suppress approaching intruders before pausing briefly to reload.

Bomber Minions are flying Collector minions featured in All 4 One. These aerial assault units possess a distinct design: a small central body dominated by a large mouth flanked by eyes, propelled by two jet units, with small arms dangling below and a rotating tailfin.
Nanophytes are enemies encountered in Tools of Destruction. They are small scavenger aliens that inhabit the lombax ruins of Fastoon and scavenge for scraps of lombax technology.
t: Nanophytes are relatively durable enemies but can be easily knocked back and avoided. Clubbers rely on overhead slams and swinging attacks, while bombers maintain distance before throwing bombs. Clubbers often appear in large groups, while bombers can be found in pairs or accompanying one another.

d: Bouncer Minions are a type of collector minions featured in All 4 One. They serve as armored melee shock troops designed to capture resilient species; for example, in the Polar Sea, a single minion nearly captured a grungoth individually. They first appear in the N.E.S.T.
t: Bouncer Minions rely exclusively on melee attacks. They can execute powerful slam attacks, fold up to perform a spinning strike while in transport mode, or release a charged electrical attack that shocks everything in their immediate vicinity. However, because all of these attacks have a limited range, they can be easily avoided by maintaining a safe distance.

d: Grubsnuckers are enemies in Tools of Destruction and Before the Nexus, and mentioned in Full Frontal Assault. They are medium-sized flying creatures with insectoid wings, native to Sargasso.
t: All grubsnucker and Breegus wasp variants attack Ratchet from a range, keeping a distance from him when firing slow-moving projectiles. Although they are found in groups, they often do not cluster too closely together, and as flying enemies, they can be hard to hit. In Tools of Destruction, if within range the Nano-Swarmers are best at taking them down, followed by either the Buzz Blades or Shard Reaper.

d: Buccaneers are enemies in Tools of Destruction and Quest for Booty, with an appearance in the comic series. They are space pirates that make use of melee weapons. Hardy buccaneers carry large shields, making them more difficult to battle.
t: Buccaneers attempt to get within range for a melee strike upon spotting Ratchet. Although they need to get close in order to inflict damage, their massive swords can take a major chunk from Ratchet's nanotech if they connect.

d: Buccaneers are enemies in Rift Apart. The most common type of space pirates, they are melee fighters with pirate swords. Shield pirates carry large shields protecitng them from frontal attacks.
t: Buccaneers attack by rushing Ratchet or Rivet and using their melee weapon. Their walking speed is close to that of Ratchet or Rivet, meaning that it is difficult to keep a distance without jumps or Phantom Dash. They can be slowed using a Cold Snap or Topiary Sprinkler, or distracted with Glove of Doom or Mr. Fungi.

d: Bursting blekkos are enemies in Into the Nexus. They are explosive lifeforms native to the Hagrow Swampland on Thram, and are first encountered during the mission "Find 10 Gargathon horns". They vaguely resemble dinosaurs.

Bury blossoms are enemies in Size Matters, with a minor appearance in Secret Agent Clank. Native to Ryllus, they are large, carnivorous flowers that spit globs of a hazardous substance at long range, or try and bite if their prey is close enough.
Cactus pirates, also known as cactus beasts, are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are ravenous cactus beasts that Captain Qwark claimed to have defeated on Hydrano during "Qwarkography, Ch. 5".

}} Canine-bots are enemies in Secret Agent Clank, fought in and outside the Boltaire Museum. They are small, canine robots from planet Edificus. Agent Clank fought them while attempting to infiltrate the Boltaire Museum to investigate the scene of the crime.

Cannonball tanks, also known as bomber tanks, are heavy armored vehicles utilized by blarg forces in Ratchet & Clank and its 2016 reimagining. They feature high durability and are equipped with double-barreled cannons for long-range bombardment.
t: In the original title, cannonball tanks function primarily as heavy obstacles that fire a rhythmic barrage of bombs. Due to their extreme toughness, high-damage ordnance such as the Devastator or the Glove of Doom is recommended to neutralize the turret quickly.

d: }} The casino guards are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are underpaid humanoid robotic guards from Kalidon that patrol Le Paradis Des Tricheurs Casino. Casino guards had the same body build as the watchman enforcement-bots, though they wear different uniforms, and were built on different planets.

Cerullean centipedes are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are multi-legged insectoids which appear in the Cerullean Sector, specifically on Cobalia and in the Nundac Asteroid Ring, often alongside Cerullean swarmers.

Cerullean swarmers are enemies in Tools of Destruction and Before the Nexus, They are small, aggressive creatures that use their teeth to attack. Named for the Cerullean Sector, Cerullean swarmers are found in locations throughout the sector, such as on Cobalia as well as others in the Polaris Galaxy.
t: Cerullean swarmers have relatively low armor and can be dispatched with a few hits. Their only danger comes in numbers, in which they can overwhelm Ratchet if he allows it. Weapons such as the Fusion Grenade, Shock Ravager, and Nano-Swarmers that can dispatch a group of enemies are ideal against them.

d: Chompers are recurring enemies in Ratchet & Clank and its 2016 reimagining. Deployed by Drek Industries, these small blargian robots feature oversized, toothy maws designed for biting. Ratchet and Clank encountered them across several planets, including Gaspar, Quartu, and Kalebo III.
t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002)=== In the original game, chompers pose a minimal threat due to their low health and limited melee range. The OmniWrench, Pyrocitor, and Walloper are highly effective at clearing swarms at close range.

d: Pygmy tribesmen are enemies in Size Matters, with a minor appearance in Secret Agent Clank. They are small, yellow, humanoid creatures that inhabit the Vetega Jungle on Ryllus, with a stripe of red paint, a tuft of red hair, a loincloth, and a large sabre.

Robot swarmers are a series of robot enemies featured in Deadlocked. They come in three varieties: Tri-Spike Swarmers, Rhyno Swarmers, and Claw Tooth Swarmers. All three are essentially robotic versions of the shrieker enemy, and are used as the most basic type of fodder in DreadZone.

Cleaner Minions are collector minions featured in All 4 One. First encountered in Luminopolis, broadcasters Pepper Fairbanks and Kip Darling speculated that the then-unidentified robots did not belong to Dr. Nefarious and might be part of another force invading the city while everyone was distracted by the Z'Grute.

Cleaner bots, also known as Rift-Jumper Minions, are enemies featured in All 4 One and Full Frontal Assault. They typically appearing as limbless robots with miniature rotor blades or sweepers beneath them, along with two antennae on top. When hostile, they deploy scythe-like arms for melee combat.
t: ===All 4 One=== Living up to their "Rift-Jumper" designation, cleaner bots are deployed through teleportation, typically arriving in large swarms. Despite their numbers, they pose a minimal threat due to their reliance on melee attacks and low durability.

d: Collector minions are enemies in All 4 One. Led by Commander Spog, they are robots that served the Loki Master, operating primarily on Magnus. They collected creatures and carried out military actions across Magnus and on other planets visited by Ephemeris.

Constructo bots, also referred to as constructorbots, are enemies featured in Ratchet & Clank and its 2016 reimagined counterpart. Located at Outpost X11 on Aridia, they are humanoid, yellow robots found around the outpost. They utilize integrated flamethrowers to repel intruders and native sandsharks.
t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002)=== In the 2002 release, constructo bots attack by sweeping their flamethrower in a wide horizontal arc. After a burst, they momentarily lift their face shields to inspect the weapon's nozzle, creating a brief window of vulnerability. While the flames can be jumped over, the attack can also be interrupted by sustaining heavy damage.

d: Corsairs are enemies in Tools of Destruction and Quest for Booty. They are space pirates that make use of long range firepower instead of the melee weapons their buccaneer counterparts use. As with buccaneers, corsairs come in a variety of appearances in their outfit and facial features.
t: Corsairs have a long range, but a low rate of fire, and are not particularly tough. It is often best to keep a distance from them and use ranged weapons such as the Combuster and Predator Launcher, or later the Buzz Blades and Negotiators against them.

d: Corsairs are enemies in Rift Apart. They are ranged space pirates that use antique musket pistols which fire in short bursts.
t: Corsairs maintain a distance from their target before firing their pistols. Their pistols fire slow-moving bullets in the air, which are telegraphed and easy to dodge, but can deal significant damage on harder difficulties. Because corsairs come in groups, their bullets can become overwhelming. Phantom Dashes and jumps can be timed to avoid them.

d: The Countess' guards are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are humanoid robots tasked with guarding Countess Ivana Lottabolts' villa on Glaciara. Clank encountered them first in "Tango of 100 Sorrows". One greeted him at the door, threatening to shoot until he presented an invitation.

Cragmite hunters are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are adult cragmites with six legs, an incredibly narrow waist, a hunchbacked body with both a long and thin neck and arms, with a gun mounted on their left arm that they can operate with their claws.

Cragmite warriors are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are larger adult cragmites with broad torsos, thick necks and long, thin arms, using shoulder-mounted guns that fire three medium-range blasts at once.

Cragpoles are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are baby cragmites who have no arms, and only four legs. Cragpoles appear in large groups, are spawned from alien spawn pods, and spawn from the bodies of fallen adult cragmite warriors and cragmite hunters.

Craterpedes are giant arthropods native to the Phonica Moon, featured as enemies in All 4 One. They resemble large centipedes with multiple blue-purple segments linked by energy beams, similar in structure to the Megapede boss from Going Commando.

Croid Bots are robotic mechs appearing in All 4 One. Designed by Dr. Croid to guard his laboratories in Terawatt Forest and on the Phonica Moon, each unit is controlled by an operator robot housed within a transparent cockpit.
t: Croid Bots utilize two primary energy attacks: volleys of blue energy projectiles and a concentrated laser beam. The laser is notably difficult to evade due to its high velocity. The most effective strategy is to engage them from a distance using high-damage weaponry such as the Warmonger. Alternatively, the Arc Lasher can be used to temporarily disable their functions, leaving them vulnerable to follow-up attacks.

d: Cutlassies are enemies in Rift Apart. They are small, hovering, ball-shaped space pirates that attack in swarms.
t: Cutlassies are swarmer enemies that attack in large groups to overwhelm Ratchet or Rivet with sheer numbers and melee attacks. As swarmer enemies, they are not durable. Cutlassies attack with a spinning attack in melee range, but there is a noticeably wind-up animation before they attack that gives a moment to dodge. It is crucial to destroy them before too many overwhelm Ratchet or Rivet in short distance.

d: Cyclobombers are enemies in A Crack in Time. They are one of four basic classes of Nefarious Troopers (alongside Splitterbots, Protoguards, and Arc Strikers), fought by Ratchet and Clank across the Breegus System of the Polaris Galaxy.
Cycloids, and Ghost Cycloids, are enemies in Deadlocked. They are spinning, hovering Vox Industries machines deployed during DreadZone battlecourses, attacking with one-armed laser cannons.

DZ Strikers are the most common enemy type produced by Vox Industries in Deadlocked. They feature as the standard foot soldiers in DreadZone, with new tournaments introducing stronger variants like the DZ Berserkers, DZ Vipers, DZ Stingers, DZ Annihilators, and DZ Ghost Strikers.
Darters are avian enemies appearing in Ratchet & Clank and its 2016 reimagining. These bat-like birds are known for diving at targets to strike with their beaks.
t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002)=== In the original game, darters are difficult to hit with the OmniWrench or Walloper due to their flight and high agility; using these short-range weapons often leaves Ratchet vulnerable to a counter-attack. It is most effective to dodge immediately as they descend into close range.

d: }} Desert dune monsters are enemies in Going Commando, encountered in the mining area on planet Tabora. They are immense, round, cycloptic, flying, orange and brown-colored monsters that hide underneath dead wood and large rocks in the dunes of the Tabora desert.

Detonoids are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are small robots that self-destruct on contact, fought in the Imperial Fight Festival challenges on Mukow. Detonoids attack by homing toward their target and starting a countdown before self-destructing.
Doctor Qwarks are enemies in Size Matters, encountered in the "??????????" mission in Dreamtime. They are nightmarish versions of Captain Qwark wearing a doctor's outfit, wielding chainsaws.

}} Doppelgangers are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. The doppelgangers were powerful robots under the command of the Kingpin who disguised themselves as Fort Sprocket's robot guards so that the Kingpin and his forces could infiltrate the Bolt Foundry.

attacks: Handgun laser, short range missile, spinning attack

d: The Dr. Croid Guardian Bots, more commonly referred to as simply guardians, are robots in All 4 One, who serve primarily as enemies, with one serving as an ally. They are large robots patented and developed by Dr. Frumpus Croid, used to guard Terawatt Forest from collector minion assaults.

attacks: Melee attacks, ion-hand cannons, fusion turrets

d: DreadZone dropships are a assault dropships in Deadlocked. They are manufactured by Vox Industries and are the primary means of transporting troops into the DreadZone gameshow, when the troops are not warped in directly.

Dreadgrubs are aggressive, caterpillar-like creatures native to the Deadgrove on planet Magnus, featured in All 4 One. While primarily found in the Deadgrove, a small number of dreadgrubs are also spawned by the Grivelnox, a creature native to Rykan V.
Drone bots are enemies in Up Your Arsenal. They are small, hovering robots that work for Dr. Nefarious, having three eyes, a thruster in place of legs, and a laser cannon in place of their right arm.

Drophyd cyclocannons are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are two-wheeled tanks in the Imperial Army, with rapid-fire laser cannons, that they sweep across the area in front of it. The cyclocannons are operated by a drophyd in a cockpit in-between the large massive wheels.

Drophyd sentries are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are drophyd infantry units fighting for the Imperial Army, equipped with nanotech combat armor and melee weapons, as opposed to their ranged drophyd trooper counterparts.
t: Drophyd sentries can deal moderate amounts of damage if they land a hit. Their slowness and moderate durability means that they pose a relatively small threat. These enemies can be defeated with ranged weapons such as the Combuster and dispatched with relative ease in groups through the Fusion Grenade.

d: Drophyd troopers are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are drophyd infantry units fighting for the Imperial Army, with nanotech combat armor and ranged weapons, as opposed to their melee drophyd sentry counterparts.
t: The gunfire from drophyd troopers is relatively easy to avoid, and their durability is not too high in comparison to other enemies. However, drophyd troopers can become cumbersome to fight when multiple are grouped together. The Fusion Grenade is strong against them in groups, but as singular enemies, the Combuster is effective; doing so will require the player to strafe to avoid their attacks, however.

d: Dropship enemies are deployed by Nefarious Troopers in A Crack in Time. Used throughout the Breegus System in the Polaris Galaxy, they are flying saucers equipped with missile launchers on either side of their cockpit.

Electroids are enemies in Ratchet & Clank. They are blargian robots manufactured on Quartu and used by Drek Industries. They were first encountered by Ratchet on Veldin after they arrived on the planet to secure the crash site.
t: Electroids are most dangerous at close range due to the limited reach of their electrical attacks and cannot redirect their aim once they begin firing. While the Bomb Glove is an effective long-range counter, players can also exploit their attack pattern. Their electrical cannons discharge for only a few seconds before the units briefly deactivate.

d: }} Megacorp gladiators are enemies in Going Commando. They are genetically engineered Megacorp aliens that fought in the Galactic Gladiators event in the Maktar Resort, while the more powerful elite Megacorp gladiators fought in the Megacorp Games event on Joba.

where: Galactic Gladiators, Maktar Resort, Maktar Nebula

t: Megacorp gladiators use their chain-mace for both short or medium range attacks. They use their shield for defense against attacks, though they will drop it on sustaining enough damage. Megacorp gladiators mostly pose a threat in large numbers, as when clustered, many can swing their chain-maces at Ratchet at once, making them harder to avoid.

d: Ratchet clones are enemies in Size Matters fought in the Clone Factory on Quodrona. They were created by Otto Destruct using the technomites' technology after extracting Ratchet's DNA on Medical Outpost Omega, in order to form an army for Destructs' nefarious deeds.
t: The standard clones using OmniWrenches have a limited range, unlike those using the Lacerator, but those lack a high rate of fire. In both cases they can be relatively easily outmameuvered and taken down. The flamethrower and shotgun-wielding variants are not too different either; while the former will be fast, they cannot move while firing their weapon, and have less health to make up for their speed.

d: Sharpshooters, also known as snipe bots, are enemies in Up Your Arsenal, fought on planet Daxx, in the Zeldrin Starport, and in the crash site on planet Zeldrin.
t: Sharpshooters mainly pose a threat due to their weapons having a powerful range to them, and being able to lay down suppressive fire from far away. They will track Ratchet with their red laser sight, and fire shortly after.

d: Enforcers are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are machines designed by Percival Tachyon for the Imperial Army, piloted by drophyds. A central piece of Tachyon's army, enforcers are used in imperial invasions, such as Tachyon's invasion of Kerwan, as well as for security.
t: Enforcers fire rapid-fire laser blasts from their cannons in bursts, before briefly recharging and firing again. Though the laser blasts can be dodged, their main threat is their durability. Enforcers can withstand a large amount of damage while dishing out some of their own.

d: Mr. Zurkon is a recurring synthenoid in the Ratchet & Clank series. Manufactured by GrummelNet, he is a line of robots with a distinct personality, known for cracking one-liners and sadistic jokes while firing his blaster at enemies. Mr.
t: ===Overview=== Mr. Zurkon, once deployed, hovers around Ratchet and fires at enemies until his ammo is depleted, at which point he self-destructs. His blasts have a moderate rate of fire and do decent damage over his lifespan, making him a very versatile weapon useful against most types of enemies. Mr.

d: Executioners are enemies in Deadlocked. They were robotic heavy-duty DreadZone soldiers wielding immense axes that could cleave opponents in two, and fire heavy bolts of energy at enemies.
Merc diver: Jacques Zissou, Stormy, Lt. Dale, Lt. James, Leary, Rexer, Dane, Chief Billy
t: The initial quartet of expatriots are encountered in a stealth scenario, and must be taken out using a takedown.

d: Extermibots are enemies in Going Commando, with a cameo in Secret Agent Clank. They are encountered in Allgon City, Damosel. They are large, heavily armored robots with a thick torso and no head, carrying either a pistol that fires electricity, or one that launches grenades that release poisonous gas.

Extermibots are robotic enemies appearing in Ratchet & Clank, the 2016 reimagined game, and the Qwark vid-comic Arriba Amoeba! in Up Your Arsenal. Deployed by the Blackwater City Administration on Rilgar to combat an amoeboid infestation, these robots are armed with gas-firing weaponry.
t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002)=== In the original Ratchet & Clank, extermibots charge toward Ratchet to discharge a short-range toxic green mist. While individually weak, they often attack in groups, which can prove overwhelming if they are allowed to close in; however, this aggression also makes them effective against amoeboids. They are vulnerable to most medium-range weaponry.

d: Extermitanks are heavily armored robotic enemies appearing in Ratchet & Clank and its 2016 reimagining.
t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002)=== Extermitanks primarily serve as environmental obstacles. They typically patrol in fixed, predictable patterns—often guarding doorways—while discharging a short-range toxic spray. Due to their limited mobility, they are easily dispatched from a distance using the Blaster. While the Glove of Doom is effective, the spawned Agents are vulnerable to the tank's spray.

d: Fendersax wasps, also known as needle wasps, are enemies in Rift Apart. They are large, invasive, flying insectoids with venomous stingers and corrosive acid. They are also a source of honey.

attacks: Long range acidic spit globs attack

t: Wasps are aggressively territorial, and move erratically through the air. They can use venomous stingers, but their primary attacks are shooting acid attacks that land on the ground, similar to the cluster bombs of the Nefarious Peacekeeper.

d: Fighters and bombers are enemy spacecraft encountered by Ratchet and the Aphelion throughout the Breegus System in A Crack in Time. They belong to the three major military factions within the System, each with distinct designs. The first fighters appear during "Defeat Vorselon's Fighters", protecting Vorselon's warship.

Flabberfish are enemies appearing in Octonok Cay and the Polar Sea, featured in All 4 One. These amphibious fish are adapted to survive and hunt outside of water; they move on land by jumping and using their fins and tail to hop towards prey.

Floranian bloody flies are enemies in Up Your Arsenal, encountered in the Nabla Forest on planet Florana, and on the outskirts surrounding the research facility on planet Daxx. They are a species of large, red flies with glowing yellow eyes, which stab foes with their stinger-shaped abdomens.

Flying hypos are enemies in Size Matters, encountered during the "??????????" mission in Dreamtime. They are strange, flying needle creatures that appear by teleporting, and will attempt to stab Ratchet.

Fungal pirates are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are space pirates that Qwark claimed to have defeated in the spaceship graveyard after they captured a group of space nuns, occurring during "Qwarkography, Ch. 4".

Fusion Turrets are turrets in Tools of Destruction. Fusion Turrets are fought as an enemy in "Search the Station" in the Apogee Space Station. They are immobile defensive turrets that normally hide under the floor, only visible as black pads.

}} Gadgetron Hounds of Cuddly Death are enemies in Going Commando, encountered in the Vukovar Canyon, Barlow. They are small, orange, dog-like creatures with a friendly appearance but hostile behavior.
Gatling turrets are enemies in Up Your Arsenal. They are spherical, rapid-fire gatling gun turrets that are used for defensive purposes.

}} Robot zombies are enemies fought in Deadlocked. As their name implies, they are undead robots fought in the sacred robot burial ground in the Catacrom Graveyard on Catacrom Four. They are bipedal, humanoid robots that can appear from the ground and can survive without their legs, or heads.
t: Robot zombies are durable enemies with strong armor and powerful melee attacks (especially on Hero difficulty). Though their movement is slow, if they are capable of surrounding Ratchet, attacking him from behind, or appearing very close to him, they can be dangerous opponents as their melee attacks can severely damage Ratchet's nanotech.

d: Robot ninjas are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. As their name suggests, they are small robotic ninjas that serve as Number Woo's private army on Asyanica. Clank fought them during "Number Woo works for...?". Later, Captain Qwark included them in his story during "Qwarkography, Ch. 1" as giant ninjas.
t: Robot ninjas attack by running up to Clank and swinging nunchuks after him. After making an attack, they will disappear with a small smoke cloud, before reappearing a distance away. They will also vanish if Clank leaves their local area, preventing him from pelting them with long-ranged attacks.

d: Giant ninjas are enemies in Up Your Arsenal fought in Lot 43, Holostar Studios. They appear during the bossfight in the mission "Film a Secret Agent Clank Episode", in the filming of the Secret Agent Clank episode, "Maxmillian Strikes Back".

Gladiators are enemies in Up Your Arsenal encountered in challenges in the Annihilation Nation on Station Q9. They are humanoid creatures with reptilian skin which is either a dark blue or greenish-yellow color, and their notable features are their large gaping jaw filled with razor-blade teeth.

The Glove of Doom is a weapon featured in Ratchet & Clank, its 2016 reimagining, Up Your Arsenal, Size Matters, and Rift Apart. The weapon's mechanical subordinates, the Agents of Doom, also appear as enemies in Secret Agent Clank.
t: ===Overview=== In all appearances, the Glove of Doom throws an egg that deploys the Agents of Doom to seek out and attack nearby enemies. It is therefore a defensive, strategic weapon, allowing the player to focus on bigger targets while the Agents supplement Ratchet's damage or attack smaller targets nearby.

d: }} Goon infantry, also known as thug shooters, are enemies in Before the Nexus, Into the Nexus, and Rift Apart. They are a basic unit of the Goons-4-Less and equip blaster pistols as their weapon.
t: ===Overview=== Goon infantry primarily attack the lombaxes by shooting from a distance, firing laser projectiles. If they get too close to their target, they will smack with their gun in a melee attack. The projectiles are telegraphed and can be avoided, but these projectiles are aimed better on harder difficulties. During hectic firefights with multiple enemies, their blaster shots can sometimes be hard to spot.

d: The goon rusher, also known as the hammer goon, or thug brawler, is an enemy in Into the Nexus and Rift Apart. It is a melee infantry unit of the Thugs-4-Less, armed with large hammers, swords, or occasionally both, with one in each hand.
t: ===Overview=== As their name and looks imply, goon rushers utilize rush tactics with melee weapons, sprinting up to Ratchet or Rivet, slashing with swords and smashing with hammers. They are somewhat durable enemies and do not pose a huge threat on their own, but can be overwhelming in large numbers. On higher difficulties, their attacks are much faster with less wind up.

d: Goons-4-Less, known as Thugs-4-Less prior to rebranding, is a mercenary organization that appears as the secondary antagonist faction in Going Commando, Into the Nexus, and Rift Apart, with minor appearances in other titles.

Gore thwogs are enemies in Quest for Booty. They are relatives of the thwog species found on Ardolis. Physically, gore thwogs possess two large, glowing red eyes with black pupils, distinguishing them from regular thwogs, which have three pupilless yellow eyes.
Gravity Minions, also known as gravity bots, are collector minions featured in All 4 One. They manipulate gravity to maintain the floating Aldaros Plains for the gravoids.
t: Gravity Minions are highly durable. Their gravity manipulation increases the player's jump height, making it easier to evade their rock barrage attacks. However, their large size and predictable attack patterns make them vulnerable. Continuous fire from the Combuster is typically sufficient to defeat them. Once destroyed, their gravitational influence in the area dissipates.

d: Gravoids are balloon-like creatures featured in All 4 One. Originally from the black rock moons of Ebaro, several were captured and transported to planet Magnus by Ephemeris.
t: When combating gravoids, speed is essential, as they may flee if not dealt with quickly. The Combuster is particularly effective due to its high rate of fire, especially in an overload attack. The Arc Lasher can temporarily stun them, though its short range and lower damage output make it a less ideal choice.

d: Gravoid Brutes are a more dangerous variant of the gravoids featured in All 4 One. Native to the black rock moons of Ebaro, they are part of a group of gravoids transported to Magnus by Ephemeris.
t: Gravoid Brutes are large and durable, capable of withstanding a few overload attacks. Despite their resilience, their missile attacks are relatively easy to evade by carefully monitoring the targeting reticules. Consistent fire from the Combuster is typically sufficient to defeat them, though the Warmonger and other strong medium-range weapons are also effective.

d: Grove beetles are large, aggressive beetles native to the Deadgrove on planet Magnus, appearing in All 4 One. They are characterized by their vibrant, multicolored shells and the large horn on their heads. Their thick, armored shell is nearly indestructible, resembling the sewer-dwelling razor ants of Ringus Minor.

}} Grulches are enemies in Going Commando encountered in the Megacorp distribution facility on Smolg. They are small, purple creatures with spiked backs, large mouths, and tiny quadrupedal legs. They are native to Smolg, and are smaller cousins of the two-headed Smolgian snapper.
Grungarian bombers, often referred to as just bombers, are aerial enemies in Full Frontal Assault. They are flying gunships used by the grungarian marauders to fire medium-range missiles.
t: Grungarian bombers attack by firing a barrage of missiles at a moderate rate. These missiles can inflict heavy damage on base barriers and generators. As flying units, they are completely immune to all mines.

d: Grungarian brawlers are enemies in Full Frontal Assault. They are melee combatants that fight for the grungarian marauders.
t: ===Overview=== Grungarian brawlers attack with a variety of tentacle moves, including smashing them together, slamming them on the ground, or performing a spinning attack. They serve as front-line foot soldiers for the marauders, either leading assaults on the player's base or patrolling key areas of the map.

d: Grungarian demolitionists, also known as launcher minions in concept art, are enemies in Full Frontal Assault. They are heavily armored grungarian marauders who attack from a distance with grenade launchers. Demolitionists have blue and white skin with a single horn protruding from the top of their head.
t: ===Overview=== Demolitionists are muscular, bipedal aliens who wield a large, shoulder-mounted grenade launcher similar to the Plasmabomb Launcher. They typically attack in pairs, firing explosive rounds from long range, and usually from an elevated position. A red targeting reticle appears on the ground just before a grenade lands, giving players a brief moment to evade.

d: The grungarian marauders are an organization and the antagonists in Full Frontal Assault. They are a mercenary army hired by Stuart Zurgo to attack planets across the Polaris Galaxy after he disabled their Planetary Defense Centers.
Grungarian soldiers, also known as soldiers or gatling minions in concept art, are enemies in Ratchet & Clank: Full Frontal Assault. They are armored grungarian marauders that serve as ranged units.
t: ===Overview=== Armed with rapid-fire gatling guns, grungarian soldiers lay down heavy fire against their enemies. While they prefer to attack from a distance, they remain dangerous in close-quarters combat. Some use jetpacks to attack from the air. They also hide behind walls to ambush enemies and fire from cover.

d: Grungarian tanks, often referred to as just tanks, are formidable enemies in Full Frontal Assault. They are heavily-armored vehicles that, upon reaching an enemy base, transform into bipedal mechs armed with dual gatling guns to inflict immense damage on generators. They are controlled by grungarian demolitionists.

where: Hidden City of Balkai, Snow Storm, Ebaro
attacks: Dual gatling guns (mech form), Crushing units (tank form)

t: ===Overview=== Grungarian tanks are protected by heavy armor that shrugs off most weapon fire. They are devastating to a base's generators but are also very slow-moving. While they largely ignore players, standing in a tank's path is dangerous, as they will flatten any units, deployed weapons, and active barriers on their way to the base.

d: Grungoids are enemies in Full Frontal Assault. They are the most common type of the grungarian marauders and serve as cheap, cannon-fodder infantry that attacks in large groups. Grungoids are the smallest and only non-bipedal grungarian subtype. They move around on eight stubby legs and have blue, green, or purple skin.
t: Grungoids attack exclusively at melee range by jumping and slamming their mace down on a target. While a single grungoid is weak, their attack hits the base generators harder than average, and a large swarm poses a serious threat if left unchecked. Fortunately, grungoids have minimal health and can be dispatched with a single hit from almost any weapon or basic defenses like the Pyro Turret.

d: The grungoid turret is an enemy in Full Frontal Assault. They are defensive turrets operated by grungoids, used to guard important areas. When no threats are nearby, the turret remains retracted underground, with only the top of the grungoid operator's helmet visible.
t: In both the campaign and multiplayer mode, grungoid turrets are used to defend key areas of interest. Their rapid-fire fusion bursts can quickly drain a player's health if they are caught in the open. The Cryoshot is uniquely suited for defeating grungoid turrets, as it can freeze them in a single hit.

d: Guard bots are enemies in Up Your Arsenal. Ratchet and Clank first fought them in the research facility on Daxx, later on the Obani Pollux moon, and finally at the crash site on Zeldrin. They are giant flying robots that patrol Dr. Nefarious' affiliated areas and fire dual machine guns from their arms.
t: Guard bots will fire their long-range machine guns at Ratchet, and their gunfire will follow him at fairly long distances. The gunfire can be dodged by running faster, and if the bots are hit with a hard enough blast, they will be temporarily staggered. They are best defeated with powerful weapons such as the Flux Rifle, Annihilator, or Disc Blade Gun, though failing this, most long-range weapons are effective.

d: Guard torsos are enemies in Size Matters fought in the Jowai Resort, Pokitaru, and in the Mechanoid Factory on Kalidon. They are green technomite robots with a broad upper body, arms that can swap into ranged laser weapons, and a Robotic Control Unit that makes up the head.

Gun turrets are enemies in Size Matters and Secret Agent Clank. In the former, they are fought in the Surgical Facility on Medical Outpost Omega, during "Escape the medical facility", and are also seen in the Clone Factory's lobby on Quodrona during "Find Otto Destruct".

}} Shadow of the Robot is the third Qwark vid-comic in Up Your Arsenal. The comic tells the story of Captain Qwark who, having chased Dr. Nefarious to his base on planet Magmos, infiltrated the base using a disguise. Nefarious saw through Qwark's disguise, and set traps waiting for him inside.

}} Henchbots are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are small, somewhat humanoid robots from Rionosis employed by numerous different criminals. Among their employers were Number Woo, the Kingpin, and those competing in Le Paradis Des Tricheurs Casino's High Stakes Room.

where: Azcotal Alley and mountainside ascent, Rionosis

t: Henchbots are small enemies that attack only with bites, and are fought as Clank or as gadgebot mk.IIs. As Clank, the Tie-A-Rang or simple melee attacks are sufficient; as the gadgebots, attacking with all gadgebots at once is ideal.

d: Homing mines are automated explosive enemies in Ratchet & Clank. They are primarily encountered at Qwark's headquarters on Umbris during "Survive Qwark's gauntlet" and within the bomb factory on Hoven during the missions "Destroy the Planetbuster" and "Explore the Icy Wastes".

Horned toads, also known as horny toads, or sand toads, are enemies in the original Ratchet & Clank, Ratchet & Clank (2016 game), and Rift Apart. They are common, carnivorous, quadrupedal amphibians typically encountered roaming in small groups.
t: Horny toads typically rely on numerical superiority and agility. Their primary attack is a melee bite, which is telegraphed by the creature pausing to face the player and letting out a loud croak.

d: Hot Heads are enemies in Quest for Booty. They are grenadiers of Angstrom Darkwater's undead pirate crew on Merdegraw.
t: Hot head pirates attack by moving around and trying to hit Ratchet with their cannon torch, and use it to light the fuse on their back to fire their own heads at him. Multiple of the launched skull heads would roll towards Ratchet and attack independently from the pirate body.

d: Hover bots are enemies in Up Your Arsenal, encountered in the Deep Sea Hideout on Aquatos during the mission "Infiltrate the underwater hideout".
Hover turrets are enemies in Going Commando, used as a defensive measure against intruders in the Deep Space Disposal Facility in the Hrugis Cloud.

Hug-Me-Tight Nanny Bots are enemies in Tools of Destruction. Fought in the Imperial Fight Festival, Mukow, they are big electric machines with immense arms, whose hands smash together to electrify an enemy.
t: Hug-Me-Tight Nanny Bots are melee only enemies and relatively slow, but are challenging due to their toughness. Because they are electrified, they are immune to the Shock Ravager. As such, it is best to prioritize them in any battle against them, attacking them with ranged weapons such as the Combuster, Plasma Beasts, or Predator Launcher before they can close in on Ratchet.

d: Hunter Minions are a variant of collector minions featured in All 4 One. First appearing in the N.E.S.T., they attack in swarms and serve as weak aerial foes.

Deja Q All Over Again was the fourth and supposedly last Qwark vid-comic in Up Your Arsenal. The story takes place in Metropolis, and depicts Captain Qwark interrupt his exercise for Helga von Streissenburgen to defend the city from an attack by Dr. Nefarious' army of insectoids.

Operators are robotic enemies encountered in All 4 One. They serve both the Collector minions and Frumpus Croid, often controlling defensive mechanisms or mechs. Known turrets they operate include the proton turret, ion turret, and the proton excavator.
t: Operators do not fight directly but instead control turrets and mechs. Their combat effectiveness depends on the machine they operate. By themselves, they are relatively weak, provided one can bypass their turret's defenses.

d: }} The Vukovar tribesmen and the related Joba tribesmen are enemies in Going Commando. They are blue-skinned, humanoid and hostile tribes native to their respective habitats, often encountered alongside their tamed saur-beasts.
t: The tribesmen either attack with their sword and shield or a deadly laser pistol. The latter is clearly visible when it is charging, as it will be flashing a bright green color, when it stops the tribesman will fire, thus requiring you to time it properly to avoid it.

d: Kamikaze droids are enemies appearing exclusively during the mission "Defeat Gleeman Vox" in Deadlocked. Deployed in batches of six by Gleeman Vox's mech, these small quadrupedal drones activate shortly after landing to charge toward Ratchet and explode on contact.

The kerchu pyroguard, is an enemy in Tools of Destruction. It is a kerchu riding a threaded vehicle equipped with two arms with twin flamethrowers. Ratchet and Clank first fought them in "Investigate the Kerchu Outpost" im Outpost L51, Sargasso, defending a gelatonium plant.
t: The pyroguard's flamethrowers can rain down fireballs from long distance, and spew a stream of flame at close range. They are very durable enemies due to their armor, but have slow movement. They are sometimes found around kerchu rollers.

d: Kerchu rollers are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are deadly kerchu wearing a backpack suit that rolls up and encompasses them in an armored, bladed ball to attack visitors on sight. Ratchet and Clank first fought them in "Investigate the Kerchu Outpost" at Outpost L51, Sargasso, defending a gelatonium plant.

Leviathans are enemies fought in Deadlocked. They are four-legged, three-eyed, giant scorpion-like creatures native to planet Sarathos. Their tails are deadly, capable of firing natural lasers or acidic goo. Ratchet and Team Darkstar fought them while being forced to compete in DreadZone.

attacks: Scorpion tail, laser beams, acid projectiles

t: Leviathans are mostly medium ranged enemies that can be very dangerous due to their strength and durability. They will either perform a sweeping laser attack or fire blasts of goo at targets. Although the former can be dodged by jumping and the latter by strafing, relying on the Holoshield Launcher is easier and safer.

d: King amoeboids are enemies featured in Up Your Arsenal. They are immense amoeboids that spit balls of slime to attack. Unlike other amoeboids, they do not split into two smaller amoeboids when defeated.
t: King amoeboids are slow enemies that attack by spitting balls of slime in medium-range. They are tough enemies that can sustain a lot of damage before being defeated. In Up Your Arsenal, they are best defeated using single-target weapons, such as the N60 Storm, Agents of Doom, Suck Cannon, or the Shock Blaster when charged up.

d: The Landstalker is both a vehicle and an enemy in Deadlocked. It is a quadrupedal tank or mech manufactured by Vox Industries for use in the DreadZone gameshow.
t: When driving the Landstalkers, the player can take advantage of their tremendous combat potential due to their firepower from their machine gun and their mortar cannons. Their limited mobility is their biggest downside, and is further exasperated by the mortars' charging time.

d: Laser Backs are large enemies featured in Deadlocked. Constructed by Vox Industries for DreadZone, they are among the largest enemies to be fought. The first Laser Back appears on "Return to the Deathbowl", after which they are a recurring foe on Torval and Maraxus, as well as several DreadZone Station challenges.

Laser bots are enemies in Up Your Arsenal encountered in challenges in the Annihilation Nation on Station Q9. They are long-range counterparts of the bash bots that fire a blue laser from a cannon attached to their arms.

Puffoids, also known as puffer fish, are enemies in Ratchet & Clank, the 2016 reimagined game, and Rift Apart. They are mutated fish with both gills and lungs, able to survive both on land and sea. Puffoids also have a variant that survive in magma known as lava puffoids.
t: In the original release, puffoids are a great threat, due to being very resilient, traveling surprisingly long distances with their hops, and attacking in large numbers. They will also attack Ratchet on the boat. Unlike most small enemies, they take two OmniWrench hits to be destroyed, making them much stronger than anticipated, and rendering the wrench ineffective against them.

d: Lawn ninjas, and lawn ninja generators, are enemies featured in Up Your Arsenal, with mentions in Going Commando, Deadlocked, and Tools of Destruction. They are Megacorp products that are used as a defense system.
t: They are small enemies with a melee attack only, and pose little threat to Ratchet. They can be dispatched with the Lava Gun or Plasma Whip quickly. When a cannon generates lawn ninjas, it should be destroyed to prevent more appearing. For Clank, lawn ninjas pose a slightly higher threat, but can be defeated using simple punches. Their attacks are fast and have decent reach, and they will backflip after attacking.

d: Lizard thugs are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are Thugs-4-Less inmates of the Prison Planet which ganged up on Ratchet along with other inmates for revenge. As with other enemies, both standard and mega variants of the thugs appeared, the mega variants first appearing in the challenge "Past Due".
t: The thugs have three means of attack: their plasma gun fires bursts of ranged shots, their sword is used when in close proximity to Ratchet, and their molotov cocktails leave fire that deals damage-over-time and is used in mid-range. The molotov cocktail is the most deadly attack as it can make the area hazardous for Ratchet, while the other attacks are simpler to avoid.

d: Lumenoids are amphibian creatures featured in All 4 One. They generate electricity and serve as a power source in Luminopolis' conduits. Normally housed inside large glass bulbs, several Lumenoids were freed when the rampaging Z'Grute broke these containers, consuming some in the process.
Lurkers are large enemies native to the Phonica Moon, featured in All 4 One. They are bulky, rotund amphibian-like creatures that typically inhabit pools of acid.

Machinegun turrets are automated sentries that appear in Ratchet & Clank and Going Commando. These static enemies spray rapid-fire bullets in a horizontal arc, rotating back and forth to cover a wide field of fire.
t: In Ratchet & Clank, the turrets on Umbris are exceptionally durable and cannot be easily destroyed through conventional damage. Striking them typically results in a temporary disablement rather than destruction. The only reliable way to permanently remove them is by using the Morph-o-Ray.

d: Robots, also known as synthetic lifeforms, are a major feature in the Ratchet & Clank series. Robots are found throughout the universe, as well as other universes, with Clank being the most notable, and come in various different forms.
Mecha-tyhrranoids are enemies encountered in Up Your Arsenal. They are two-legged mechs operated by two-eyed tyhrranoids and equipped with twin lasers.

where: Korgon Base and Kavu Island, Tyhrranosis

t: to block an ultra mecha-tyhrranoid's laser.]] The mecha-tyhhrranoid is in its earliest green-armored instance a weak enemy that is easily taken down with the Shock Blaster, simply keep wary of their beams that travel along the ground.

d: Medic bots are enemies in Size Matters, fought in the Surgical Facility, Medical Outpost Omega. They are surgery robots that extracted Ratchet's DNA to create Ratchet clones, and later defended the facility.

Mega bots are enemies in Up Your Arsenal. They are immense, humanoid robots with thick armor, working for Dr. Nefarious. They have a dark red color, orange visors in place of a face, similar to the soldier bots, missile launchers on their backs, and wrist-mounted rapid-fire lasers.

where: Starship Phoenix Nefarious BFG area, Koros

d: Maktar Resort, Maktar Nebula Thugs-4-Less jamming array Canal City, Notak Flying lab, Aranos v2.0: Testing facility, Dobbo Megacorp Armory, Todano Silver City, Boldan
t: Chickenbots will run towards a target and bite them quickly. Their durability is very low, and their attacks are melee only, meaning they serve little threat. For v1.0 Chickenbots, the Lancer and Chopper are very effective against them, and the latter can kill multiple Chickenbots at once, and also damage any other enemies nearby.

d: }} Megacorp Hover Tanks are enemies in Going Commando, encountered at the testing facility on planet Dobbo, the Thug HQ on Snivelak, and the Protopet Factory on Yeedil. Produced by Megacorp, they are heavily-armored tanks that hover above ground.
t: ===Going Commando=== against two tanks at Megacorp HQ.]] Megacorp Hover Tanks are very well armored and can sustain a lot of damage before being destroyed. Their cannon is a rapid-fire plasma cannon that fires projectiles that reach a relatively long distance before exploding upon reaching maximum range.

d: }} Megacorp Laser Bots are enemies in Going Commando. They are medium-sized yellow Megacorp robots designed to remove "hard to clean" stains and ensure public areas are clean and sanitary.

}} Megacorp Rivet Bots are enemies in Going Commando, with a cameo in Secret Agent Clank. They are large, black, bulky Megacorp-manufactured robots with a thruster in place of feet. They were designed to aid in construction, with some modified to also function as security robots.

}} Megacorp Robot Guards are enemies in Going Commando, encountered in the Megacorp Armory on Todano, as well as the distribution facility on Smolg. They are large robot guards, with a thick and heavily armored torso, a single red eye, thrusters in place of legs, and a long-ranged blaster cannon on their right arm.

n: Megacorp Security Robot I - Chainsaw Model
d: }} The Megacorp Security Robot I - Chainsaw Model, also known as the MSR type 1, is an enemy in Going Commando. It is a Megacorp robot used for security, often deployed alongside the Megacorp Security Robot II - Flamethrower Model and the PX6 BladeBall.

where: Galactic Gladiators, Maktar Resort, Maktar Nebula

t: The v1.0 MSR chainsaw model is a weak enemy, as it is fairly slow to reach Ratchet and will only be able to attack in melee range. It only ever poses a threat if a group is allowed to reach Ratchet. It is easily dispatched with a few Lancer bullets to destroy it before it even comes close, and failing this, a Gravity Bomb can destroy a group instantly.

n: Megacorp Security Robot II - Flamethrower Model
d: Galactic Gladiators, Maktar Resort, Maktar Nebula Frozen base, Siberius Megacorp Games, Joba

where: Galactic Gladiators, Maktar Resort, Maktar Nebula

t: The v1.0 MSR flamethrower model is slightly more difficult than the MSR chainsaw model, due to its longer range and wider arc of attack, and the fact that it does not stop after hitting Ratchet, giving the player less time to recover. However, the strategy for dealing with it is the same: a few Lancer bullets will destroy it before it comes close, and the Gravity Bomb can destroy a cluster in one shot.

d: }} Megacorp Security Turrets are enemies in Going Commando fought in the testing facility, Dobbo. They are small, red and silver-colored, stationary Megacorp turrets with six antenna used to create a slow moving plasma line that protects hallways from intruders.

}} Megacorp Sentinels, also known as sentinel bots, are minor enemies in Going Commando and Up Your Arsenal. They are Megacorp products that hover above the ground with a searchlight for detecting intruders, and fire turrets beneath them upon finding them.
t: In Going Commando, Megacorp Sentinels are durable opponents, and can be difficult to deal with due to their rapid rate of fire and the height at which they hover. They only attack enemies that enter their searchlights, meaning they can be somewhat avoided. If an enemy has been detected but remains outside of the lights they will repeatedly attempt to find it again.

d: }} Megacorp Sweeper Bots are enemies in Going Commando, encountered in Megapolis on planet Endako. They are small, yellow, Megacorp robots designed to clean the streets. They were also used in the testing facility on Dobbo, to clean up the mess after Megacorp Security Turrets destroyed intruders.

}} Megacorp Troopers are enemies in Going Commando. They are humanoid robot soldiers that form the vanguard of Megacorp's security forces, they are armed with dual plasma pistols, and are trained in group fighting.
t: Megacorp Troopers are well armored, making them durable, and their rapid fire plasma shots can deal a decent amount of damage if they land, meaning it is important to keep strafing and performing evasive maneuvers around them. Troopers operate in a unit, and use blocks for cover, and will perform advanced skills such as shooting while moving.

d: Megacorp gladiators appear as enemies in Secret Agent Clank, as inmates of the Prison Planet. They gang up against Ratchet along with his other foes to attack him in prison out of revenge for putting them in there. As with other foes fought in the prison, they have larger, mega variants.
t: Megacorp gladiators have greater toughness than the tyhrranoids, but less variety of attacks than the lizard thugs. Ultimately, their main threat is that they can overwhelm Ratchet in large numbers, especially combined with their lunging attacks.

d: }} Megaliths is an enemy in Secret Agent Clank. Clank encountered megalithses guarding Klunk's underwater base on Hydrano.

Microdrones are enemies in A Crack in Time. They are small Nefarious Troopers that use bolts of electricity to attack. At times, three of them will also merge, forming either a Splitterbot or a Protoguard. Ratchet and Clank fought them in various missions across the Breegus System.
Mine layers are robotic enemies in the original Ratchet & Clank. Developed by Drek Industries and utilized by the blarg, these small, humanoid units were deployed in Metropolis on planet Kerwan.

Mini-ninja henchmen are enemies in Up Your Arsenal fought in Lot 43, Holostar Studios. They only appear a few times during the mission "Film a Secret Agent Clank Episode", in which they attack Clank and Skrunch in the Secret Agent Clank episode, "Maxmillian Strikes Back".

Minibombers are enemies deployed by Drek Industries in Ratchet & Clank. They are automated aerial units, and serve as localized defense platforms within Gorda City on planet Oltanis and are encountered during the missions "Find the survivors of the blarg attack" and "Purchase Gadgetron PDA from 'Steve'".
t: Minibombers possess high durability, requiring three hits from the Devastator to be neutralized. The Visibomb Gun is highly effective at long range, allowing the player to destroy units before they can begin their bombing run. Alternatively, due to their fixed firing patterns, it is possible to simply dodge the falling ordnance and ignore the craft entirely.

d: Missile Minions are enemies featured in All 4 One and Full Frontal Assault. They serve as heavy durable aerial assault units, attacking targets with barrages of missiles. In All 4 One, they appear as collector minions, while in Full Frontal Assault, they are used by the grungarian marauders.
t: ===Overview=== Although capable of flight, Missile Minions primarily use this to approach targets and keep a fixed distance, rather than rapid repositioning. Their sole method of attack involves launching a series of missiles in quick succession. These projectiles target the area where the player was standing at the moment of firing, necessitating constant movement and strafing to avoid damage.

d: Missile Turrets are enemies featured appearing in Vox Industries' DreadZone in Deadlocked. They first appear in Kronos' "Night Flight", and subsequently on Shaar, Orxon, Stygia, and Maraxus.

The Monsterpedia is a help feature in Going Commando. It catalogs most enemies encountered by Ratchet and Clank, providing descriptions of their origins alongside statistics regarding their health, defense, toughness, and damage output.
Mortar Minions are a variant of collector minions featured in All 4 One. First appearing in the Deadgrove, they frequently serve as long-range support for Scout Minions and other enemy units.
t: Mortar Minions telegraph their attacks with a targeting reticule, though their blast radius is slightly larger than indicated. Their low rate of fire makes them relatively easy to evade while returning fire. However, the late-game variant is significantly more dangerous, launching multiple explosives in rapid succession to saturate an area.

d: }} Mutant fireflies, also known as mutant swamp flies, are enemies in Going Commando. They are small, yellow, glowing mutant fireflies native to Oozla, found in the Megacorp Outlet area, that are a cross between a firefly and a beetle.
t: Mutant fireflies are found in groups, often alongside the mutant muckdweller and mutant swamp beasts, and will circle an area before being approached.
