Once struck down, their yellow glow will end as they fall. Mutant fireflies pose little threat, as they are slow, and can be defeated easily with a hit from any weapon.

d: }} Mutant muckdwellers are enemies in Going Commando. They are small, reddish, three-eyed mammalian mutant creatures with long ears native to Oozla, found near the Megacorp Outlet area. They move by bouncing across their ground, as they have small, stubby legs.

}} Mutant swamp beasts are enemies in Going Commando encountered in the Megacorp Outlet area on planet Oozla. They are medium sized beasts that have the body of a large snail, a single eye stalk, and four tentacles with crab-like claws that swipe at enemies by plunging to attack them.

}} Mutant test-squirrels are enemies in Going Commando, encountered in the Megacorp Armory on Todano. They are large and aggressive mutated squirrels, with dark red fur, a yellow belly and yellow stripes on their tail, and a blue tongue. Native to Todano, they were originally used by Megacorp for weapons testing.
t: Mutant test-squirrels are relatively small enemies, but are surprisingly durable and can deal a decent amount of damage if they overwhelm Ratchet. While most are found over the ground, several will drop out of the trees and even attack the tourists, specifically those at the rear of the line. Ideal weapons of defense are the Minirocket Tube, Bouncer, and Plasma Coil, as they do strong damage in an area of effect.

d: Nabla natives are enemies in Up Your Arsenal, found in the Nabla Forest, Florana, encountered during the missions "Find the Mysterious Man", "Walk the PATH OF DEATH!", and "Defeat Captain Qwark". They are hostile humanoid tribesmen who wear large wooden masks and wield bladed boomerangs as their main weapon.
t: All natives use the same three-sided bladed boomerang as their only weapon. Natives will focus on either melee or ranged attacks. Melee nabla natives will simply charge towards Ratchet and swing their boomerang to attack, and will after striking take a second to look around, opening them up to a counter.

d: Nefarious Blitztrooper is an enemy featured in Rift Apart. It is a type of Nefarious Trooper bot armed with twin quad-blasters. They are a heavy ranged aerial enemy units that will keep a distance from Ratchet or Rivet and fire rapid-fire blasters.
t: Bliztrooper's main attacks are gatling gun laser arms, that deliver extremely dense rapid laser fire. Though their shots aren't as powerful as the Lastrooper's lasers and individual shots are easier to dodge, their larger quantity makes them over all more diffiuclt to evade. They also remain airborne at all times, hovering over the battlefield, and thus can pin Ratchet or Rivet down easily with their gun fire.

d: Nefarious Lasertrooper is an enemy featured in Rift Apart. It is a type of Nefarious Trooper bot armed with twin ion-flux lasers. They are a ranged enemy unit that will keep a distance from Ratchet or Rivet before firing their twin lasers.
t: Lasertroopers fire two consecutive long-range beams. Their beams begin aimed at the ground, then do a vertical sweep towards their enemies, alternating between arms each sweep. On higher difficulties their sweep is much faster and harder to anticipate.

d: Nefarious Peacekeeper is an enemy featured in Rift Apart. It is a type of Nefarious Trooper patrol vehicle piloted by a pair of Nefarious Trooper heads, equipped with a field cannon as its main weapon. Peacekeepers are primarily mid-to-long range enemies with heavy armor.
t: The Nefarious Peacekeeper is a heavy duty flying unit that fires neutron bombs at red target reticles on the ground. When they explode, they will leave a neutron field for several seconds before dissipating, and thus should be avoided as the neutron field can damage the player.

d: Nefarious Slugger is an enemy featured in Rift Apart. It is a type of Nefarious Trooper armed with mega-mass maces to each arm. It is a melee unit that will attack Ratchet or Rivet at close range after closing distance with hi,.
t: Nefarious Sluggers attack either with a punch or a slam attack with their wrecking ball-like fists. They are more heavily armored than Lasertroopers and more durable, and their walking speed is faster than Ratchet or Rivet can move while firing their weapon. As such, their main threat is overwhelming Ratchet or Rivet by closing distance on them first. On harder difficulties, their attacks are faster with less windup.

d: Nefarious Sniperbot is an enemy featured in Rift Apart. It is a flying Nefarious Trooper unit that uses devastating, fusion-drive cannons to attack from a long distance.
t: The Sniperbot is a flying unit that aims its sensor beam at a target, before them charging up a blast of its fusion-drive cannon. Avoiding the sensor beam by using cover, or timing a jump or Phantom Dash for right when it charges, is the best way to dodge its attacks.

d: Nefarious Trooper heads are enemies featured in Rift Apart and are the most basic unit of the Nefarious Troopers. While often appearing as standard enemies, every type of Nefarious Trooper can eject their heads when their primary body is destroyed to continue the fight.

Nefarious Troopers are a type of enemy in A Crack in Time. They are robots that served Dr. Nefarious in the Polaris Galaxy during his campaign to take control of the Great Clock. Nefarious Troopers were built within and had a hold on much of the Breegus System, serving as the Doctor's main army.

The Nefarious Troopers are the robotic enforcers of the Nefarious Empire in Rivet's dimension and fiercely loyal followers of Emperor Nefarious, a dimensional counterpart of Dr. Nefarious. Their collective forces make up the Nefarious Army, and are the primary enemy faction of Rift Apart, fought by Ratchet and Rivet.
Netherbeasts are enemies in Into the Nexus. They are the primary type of nethers that, when in Ratchet's dimension, assume an armored humanoid form.
t: Netherbeasts in Ratchet's dimension teleport around the battlefield and shoot at Ratchet and Clank. The elite netherbeasts are also capable of throwing an energy boomerang when at close range (similar to Ratchet's OmniWrench throw).

d: }} Nidbots are enemies in Going Commando, fought in the Megacorp Games gladiator battles on Joba. They are small insectoid robots, modeled after spiders, but with only six legs and one single red eye, as well as two antennae on top. They are made out of a dark blue metal and are sold by Megacorp to the public.

Ninja bots are enemies in Up Your Arsenal. They are robot ninjas wielding double-bladed laser swords and shurikens. Many are fought in Annihilation Nation challenges, while others are affiliated with Dr. Nefarious and fought in the Zeldrin Starport, in the Leviathan, and during an attack on the Starship Phoenix.
t: Melee ninja bots that use their swords are particularly mobile enemies that can be overwhelming in certain circumstances, as they are harder to keep up with and attack in groups. Ranged ninja bots, on the other hand, fight from safe distances, making them harder to defeat. However, other than their mobility, they are not especially tough to most weapons.

d: }} Ninja masters are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. Along with robot ninjas, they served in Number Woo's private army, and were fought by Clank during "Number Woo works for...?". Ninja masters were larger, red versions of the normal robot ninjas, with more powerful attacks.
Nurse robots are enemies in Size Matters, encountered in the Medical Outpost Omega and in the Clone Factory on Quodrona. They are humanoid robots wearing nurse outfits, carrying large syringes.

Old training robots are enemies in Size Matters, encountered in the Jowai Resort on Pokitaru. They are rusty humanoid robots wearing Hawaiian shirts and hats, with an attached spring boxing glove and peg-leg in place of their right limbs, and a built-in meter on their chest.

The one-eyed tyhrranoid was a type of tyhrranoid encountered in Up Your Arsenal, with appearances in Deadlocked and Secret Agent Clank. Considered the weakest version, they rely solely on numbers to attack opponents.
t: Being the weakest type of tyhrranoid, they are effectively dispatched with a single OmniWrench swing or with the use of any weapon, though preferably one more capable of defeating multiple weaker enemies at once, such as the Shock Blaster, Plasma Whip, or Lava Gun. They are also very useful for providing ammo for the Suck Cannon. Their attack is a short-ranged bite, which can be countered by dodging.

d: Paladrones are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are gladiators encountered at the Imperial Fight Festival, related to the argonoids and terraklons. In Tools of Destruction.
Peckbots are robotic enemies that appear in the original Ratchet & Clank and the 2016 reimagining.
t: Peckbots engage targets by charging forward with their jaws open. Before delivering a strike, they momentarily cease movement—though they remain capable of rotating toward the player—and then snap their jaws shut with a loud mechanical clank. Due to their limited durability and reliance on melee-range offense, they are easily neutralized with the OmniWrench or the Pyrocitor.

d: Pincer Rays are robotic manta ray enemies featured in Deadlocked. They are constructed by Vox Industries for the purpose of hovership challenges in DreadZone, and are only featured in "Night Flight" on Kronos and both "Space Ace" and "Time Extension!" on the Valix Belt.

The PlanetBuster Maximus is a weapon that appears in Ratchet & Clank. Manufactured by Drek Industries, it was a giant missile built in the blargian bomb factory on Hoven, carried by a large starship, and designed to destroy a planet for Chairman Drek.

defense: Five turrets on carrier ship, blarg heli-commander defenders

d: Plasmabots are specialized blargian security robots deployed by Drek Industries in Ratchet & Clank.
t: The Glove of Doom is the most effective counter to Plasmabot groups, as it deploys multiple agents to dismantle the robots simultaneously. The Bomb Glove is also a viable option, as its blast radius can neutralize units before they enter their firing range. While the Devastator is capable of destroying a Plasmabot in a single shot, its high ammo cost makes it a less efficient option.

d: Protoguards are enemies in A Crack in Time and Before the Nexus. They are one of four basic classes of Nefarious Troopers (alongside Splitterbots, Arc Strikers, and Cyclobombers), fought by Ratchet and Clank across the Breegus System of the Polaris Galaxy.

Protomantises are enemies in A Crack in Time. They are an advanced class of Nefarious Troopers, characterized by their bulky bodies, four small legs, and gatling guns as weapons. Ratchet and Clank encounter them throughout the Breegus System in the Polaris Galaxy.

Psy-tcopuses are enemies in Ratchet & Clank found in the Jowai Resort on Pokitaru. They also make a brief cameo in Deadlocked. These mutated aquatic creatures are characterized by their ability to project energy spheres from their exposed brains.
t: Individually, psy-tcopuses pose a minimal threat as their long-range energy blasts are slow and easily avoided. They become more dangerous when supported by swarms of puffoids. An effective strategy involves using the Suck Cannon to vacuum puffoids and launch them back at the psy-tcopus. Due to their lack of mobility, they are also highly vulnerable to the Bomb Glove or standard strikes from the OmniWrench.

d: Pyromites are explosive enemies encountered in All 4 One. They are small, spherical drones launched from Pyromite generators — large circular devices resembling mechanical eyeballs.

Pyrospinners are enemies in A Crack in Time and Before the Nexus. They are small hovering robots that attack by spinning slowly and using a flamethrower attached to their arms, which circles them. Pyrospinners are identical to thermosplitters, except for the flamethrowers.

Pythors are enemies in Quest for Booty native to Merdegraw. They are large insectoid creatures characterized by a thick carapace, several segmented legs, and the ability to levitate similarly to a basilisk leviathan. Pythors attack by spitting fireballs from their mouths.
Qwark bots, or Qwarkbots, are robot replicas of Captain Qwark featured in Ratchet & Clank, Up Your Arsenal, and the 2016 reimagined game.
t: In Up Your Arsenal, Qwark bots pose a significant threat due to their durability, armor, numbers, and firepower. They spawn in groups via teleportation, often on dangerous icy terrain.

d: The Qwark mech is a boss in Full Frontal Assault. It is a mech suit built in the image of Captain Qwark by his former superfan, Stuart Zurgo. Zurgo originally designed the suit when he still idolized Qwark and hoped to be his sidekick, but he later repurposed it for his revenge plot.
t: The Qwark mech's combat strategy revolves around its powerful, front-facing energy shield, which makes it invulnerable to direct attacks. The shield is powered by an exposed versa-fuse on the mech's back; destroying this fuse temporarily disables the machine. For offense, it uses a rapid-fire fission blaster and can launch missile barrages that set the terrain ablaze.

d: Razorbacks are enemies in Size Matters encountered within the Vetega Jungle on planet Ryllus during the mission "Investigate the artifact". These blue, feline creatures are characterized by red eyes and prominent red spikes along their spines.

Razormoths are enemies in All 4 One. These purple- or orange-colored, squid-like aerial creatures have bodies dominated by a large head and multiple tentacles. Their flight is facilitated by a usually concealed tail and webbed tentacles at the rear of the head.

Reapers are an aggressive race of bipedal, muscular reptile-like beings featured in both Deadlocked and Secret Agent Clank. In the former, they first appeared in "The Tower of Power" challenge in the DreadZone Battledome, and thereafter in subsequent tournaments as well as in Maraxus' Prison.
t: From afar they will stand still and fire a series of spikes from their back, which then arc downwards onto the target area. Up close they can also belch acid, although this is severely lacking in range compared to the spikes. They often appear alone or in pairs, and generally have enough toughness they cannot be taken out instantly.

d: }} Receiver Bots are robots in Going Commando. They appear both as enemies and some as units controlled by the Hypnomatic. They are created by Megacorp, Ratchet and Clank encountered them in the Tundor Wastes, Grelbin, in Allgon City, Damosel, and in the Protopet Factory, Yeedil.
t: Receiver Bots, when fought as Ratchet, are not particularly durable but are often very numerous. The v1.0 version is essentially a non-threat and is easy prey to either the Sheepinator or Shield Charger. The non-controllable v3.0 model is more dangerous and can unleash a rapid burst of blasts from both its cannons, which deal heavy damage.

d: Robomutts are enemies in Ratchet & Clank, the 2016 reimagined game, and Rift Apart. They are blargian robotic canines created by Drek Industries that travel in groups.
t: Robomutts, upon detecting an enemy, will bark loudly, and if reachable, charge towards them and bite. After their first bite, hit or miss, they will then pause slightly before attacking the next enemy, though on Kerwan in the original release, they will instead return to their original position before attacking again.

d: Tyhrranoid saucers are enemies encountered in Up Your Arsenal. They are small, flying vehicles operated by two-eyed tyhrranoids, and predominantly seen defending the Korgon Base on Tyhrranosis and during all Galactic Ranger operations on the battlefield.

where: Korgon Base and Kavu Island, Tyhrranosis

t: The Saucer appears to be quite mobile, but in effect only use this to get into position instead of dodging enemy fire. They often appear from beneath bridges or fly in over walls, making them sometimes unpredictable. They can also teleport in one-eyed tyhrranoids on the ground beneath them, but being damaged interrupts and stops the process.

d: Robosquawkers are robotic avian enemies in Ratchet & Clank that serve as security units for Drek Industries. They are exclusively encountered within the Gemlik Base in the Oltanis orbit during the mission "Explore base". Their combat behavior is largely identical to that of peckbots.
t: Robosquawkers possess low durability and are generally considered a minor threat. They can be efficiently dismantled with standard OmniWrench strikes or short-range weapons like the Pyrocitor and Suck Cannon.

d: Robotic Control Units, or R.C.U.s, are enemies in Size Matters fought throughout the game. They are technomite robots comprised of a head moved by six spider legs, which control the guard torso and technomite heavy trooper units, and can also take command of gun turret security.
t: Robotic Control Units are vulnerable to the OmniWrench 10K, as well as any other weapon due to how weak they are. The Lacerator at first, and later the Scorcher and Suck Cannon, are effectively against single targets and small groups, with the Acid Bomb Glove being better against the larger groups.

d: The space pirates are a recurring organization in the Ratchet & Clank series. With their first appearance in Up Your Arsenal, their first prominent appearance is in Tools of Destruction as secondary antagonists, before appearing as the main antagonists of Quest for Booty, and as cameos in subsequent titles.

Rocket tanks are enemies in Ratchet & Clank, encountered on Veldin during "Save Ratchet's planet", in which they patrol in key locations. Manufactured by Drek Industries, these blargian tanks attack at a formidable range and rate of fire, though their accuracy is lackluster.

}} Sargasso spores, also known as Volatilis Inflatus, are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are mature organic spores from the Sargasso Reach who drift through the cosmos, many wound up in the spaceship graveyard, with Clank encountering them there during "Tracking the Kingpin".

Escape from Slag's Clutches is a mission in Tools of Destruction, taking place at the Verdigris Black Hole in the Verdigris Sector. The Aphelion is ambushed by space pirates while en route to Jasindu, as Captain Slag deduces from their flight path that Jasindu must be the location of the Dimensionator.
The Savali spitter is an enemy in Rift Apart. Native to Savali, they are large, crab-like creatures found around the Urfdah Mesa that possess ranged spit attacks and strong bite attacks.
t: Savali spitters are typically fought in groups of 2-3. At a distance they will begin spitting acid blobs, and up close they will attempt to bite. They are also quite durable. Keeping distance is recommended, as their spit attacks are easier to avoid than their melee attacks.

d: Sawbots are enemies in Ratchet & Clank. They are small, blargian, hovering, yellow robots with two sawblades for hands, used by Drek Industries. They were encountered by Ratchet and Clank in the logging site on Eudora, during the mission "Explore the mills".

Scout Minions are collector minions featured in All 4 One. They were first seen in Luminopolis, where one was grabbed and thrown by the Z'Grute. Scout Minions serve as common shock troops throughout the game, frequently appearing alongside other enemy types.

Scoutbots, also known as scout bots, are robotic enemies in Ratchet & Clank and Up Your Arsenal. They function as a mobile security force that patrols designated areas and attacks intruders with electrical shocks. These units serve both the blarg forces under Chairman Drek and Dr. Nefarious's robotic army.

where: Up Your Arsenal: Research facility, Daxx

t: ===Single player=== In both appearances, Scoutbots possess low durability and can be destroyed with a single strike from most weapons. While they deal minimal damage, their attack range is slightly longer than that of typical small melee enemies. They are vulnerable to the Suck Cannon, which can convert them into ammunition. In Up Your Arsenal, the Plasma Whip is especially effective for clearing groups.

d: Screamers are avian enemies in Ratchet & Clank that inhabit the Kogor Refinery on planet Orxon. They act as biological sentries, waking up nearby sleeping toxic crabs upon detecting nearby activity.
t: Screamers possess very low durability and can be neutralized with a single strike. Utilizing the Blaster or the OmniWrench's comet-strike to kill a screamer before it can alert nearby enemies allows the player to bypass toxic crabs without engaging them.

d: Scuttle crabs are enemies in Size Matters fought in the Jowai Resort, Pokitaru. They are a species of large, blue crabs with a single eye, presumably native to the planet.

}} Secu-tanks are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are top-of-the-lone security robots from planet Edificus. Similar to watchman robots, they are humanoid in shape, but use treads for movement and a rocket launcher on their right arm, with a specialized gun that fires a corrosive ink that only affects metals.
Security cameras, also known as CCTV cameras, are floating drones which appear at many high security locations.

Security drones are enemies in Size Matters encountered in the Mechanoid Factory on Kalidon during the objective "Search the factory". These floating robots patrol the facility in packs, utilizing searchlights to scan for intruders.

Security satellites are enemies in A Crack in Time. Found throughout the Breegus System of the Polaris Galaxy, they are satellites spread throughout space sectors with holo-net relays that they use to summon fighters. Security satellites summon a set of enemies and are initially invincible due to a shield.

Seekers are enemies in Ratchet & Clank. Deployed by Drek Industries as mobile explosives, they are encountered in the blarg depot on Gaspar during the mission "Find the Pilot's Helmet" and at the Gadgetron site on Kalebo III during "Get past the blarg".

}} The senior guard, identified as Grecko, is a minor enemy in Secret Agent Clank. A humanoid robot from Kalidon, the senior guard was tasked with carrying the Eye of Infinity during "Paradise Exploited" at the Le Paradis Des Tricheurs Casino to the high stakes room, where it was gambled on by participants.
Sentry Minions are stationary collector minions featured in All 4 One. They act as surveillance units found in the N.E.S.T. and Uzo City regions.

Sentry-bots (also spelled sentrybots) are specialized security units in Ratchet & Clank. Manufactured by Drek Industries on planet Quartu, they were intended to be the standard model produced by the factory that accidentally created the defective unit, Clank.
t: Sentry-bots typically guard forcefields that require specific clearance; Ratchet must wave while disguised in the Hologuise to trick the bots into deactivating the barriers. If a Sentry-bot is provoked or spots an intruder, it will trigger an alarm that deploys a continuous stream of homing energy spheres until the player is defeated or leaves the vicinity.

d: Serathoids are enemies in Into the Nexus. They are small, three-eyed, arachnid-like creatures, with two limbs sporting massive spikes used to attack prey. Serathoids inhabit the Zarkov Sector of the Azeril Caverns, usually in dark and damp places.

Shard beasts are mutated creatures encountered in the Terawatt Forest on planet Magnus in All 4 One. Originally native predators, they possess the unique ability to absorb energy from crystalline shards apparently energized by Toranux, dramatically increasing their size and durability.
t: Upon engaging enemies, a Shard beast typically seeks to empower itself by absorbing energy from nearby crystal deposits or growths. Once charged, it may plunge its claws into the earth to generate volleys of electrified crystal spikes that erupt from the ground around its targets. It also crawls slowly towards opponents to attack them directly with physical strikes.

d: }} Shark-a-anglers (Expiscor Exemplar) are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. Residing in the depths of Hydrano's ocean, they have the appearance of an angler fish variant of the sharkigator, with their name indicating an apparent relation to said creature.

Sharkigators, also referred to as sewer sharks or pool sharks are enemies in Ratchet & Clank, the 2016 reimagined game, Going Commando, Up Your Arsenal, Size Matters, and Rift Apart. They are hostile fish-like creatures that swim in the waters and will swallow Ratchet and Clank if they stray too close to them.
Shock troopers are enemies in Size Matters fought in the Technomite City on Challax. They are small, armored technomite foot soldiers that attack using a baton in melee range.

Shriekers are enemies in Deadlocked. They are small, green aliens native to Sarathos, with only a head, two feet, spiked tails, and giant fangs in place of their eyeholes. Ratchet and Team Darkstar first fought them in the Sarathos challenges on DreadZone, before they later appeared in the challenges on Maraxus.
Skull Walkers, also known as pirate walkers, are enemies in Quest for Booty. They are large walking space pirates used by Angstrom Darkwater's undead pirate crew on Merdegraw.
t: The Skull Walker's primary challenge is its durability rather than its firepower. Though its blasts are strong, they are relatively easy to avoid and come in fewer numbers. Skull Walkers also attack by trying to crush Ratchet if he runs under its legs.

d: Snatchers are enemy vehicles piloted by space pirates in Tools of Destruction. They are heavy fighter crafts used to attack and plunder vessels. Ratchet and Clank fought them while flying Aphelion in "Evade the Pirate Fleet" in the Rakar Star Cluster.

Soldier bots are enemies in Up Your Arsenal fought throughout the game. They are sentinel humanoid robots affiliated with Dr. Nefarious which guard various planets of importance, fought various times by Ratchet and Clank.
t: Soldier bots from range fire a burst rifle, which normally fires a burst of five slow-moving plasma bullets before firing again. Normally they hide behind cover to fire, though they sometimes fire while still marching. When in close quarters, they will instead whack Ratchet with the bayonet of their rifle.

n: Booty is in the Eye of the Beholder
d: Booty is in the Eye of the Beholder, also known as Pirate Booty!, is the first Qwark vid-comic in Up Your Arsenal. The comic tells the story of Captain Qwark fighting robotic pirate ghosts led by Captain Blackstar and his robotic space eel.
Space wasps are enemies in Going Commando. These orange, insectoid creatures possess bat-like wings and can survive in the vacuum of space, where they expel hazardous gas to damage enemy vessels.

Spawners are enemies in Going Commando. They are light-gray and pink-colored creatures, with short stubby legs and four protrusions near their sole orifice on the top. Both of their legs and protrusions are tinted a dark brown.
t: As their name implies, the spawner's sole function is to spawn new creatures, up to a limit of six at a time. If the total number of species that it spawns exceeds or is equal to that number, then it will be docile and harmless. Once that number does go below six, then they will instantly release more enemies continuously until defeated.

d: }} Spider divers are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. The robots are upgraded spider-bots equipped with a plasma based firearm on one arm, and two prison shivs on the other.
t: Both types of spider divers fired bolts of plasma at intruders, and could use their prison shivs to stab at close range. The mega variant also utilized a large laser blast that it fired from one side to another. Although their ranged attacks were strong and accurate, the real threat was the mega variant being too strong to take down quickly.

d: }} Spitting dune crawlers are enemies in Going Commando, encountered in the mining area on Tabora. They are medium-sized, quadrupedal, cycloptic creatures that spit poisonous gas in a short range from their circular jaws.

Splitterbots are enemies in A Crack in Time. They are one of four basic classes of Nefarious Troopers (alongside Protoguards, Arc Strikers, and Cyclobombers), fought by Ratchet and Clank across the Breegus System of the Polaris Galaxy.

}} Static midges are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are small red and silver robots from Metalis. The midges have sirens built into their faces which they use to alert and summon allies if they spot Clank.
t: The midges' primary strength is their numbers, with which they attempt to overwhelm their opponents, especially when one of them suddenly speeds up and rushes you. Due to this the Tie-A-Rang and Cufflink Bomb are good at handling groups, while the Holo-Knuckles and Blowtorch Briefcase are enough for handling small numbers. The Tanglevine Carnation is also useful in thinning out large groups.

d: }} Stuart Zurgo, also known as the Fan Boy or the Armory Employee, is a minor character in Going Commando and the main antagonist of Full Frontal Assault.

Swabs are enemies in Tools of Destruction and Quest for Booty. They are large, electrified, hunchbacked space pirates who attack at melee range. Swabs are heavily armored, and combined with their speed and electrification (making them immune to the Shock Ravager and Mag-Net Launcher) are very deadly.
Swamp monsters are enemies in Up Your Arsenal, encountered in the Nabla Forest on Florana, during the mission "Find the Mysterious Man".

Tachyon gunships are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are floating hoverships in the Imperial Army piloted by drophyds, named for Emperor Tachyon. Gunships are used both in invasions and defense purposes, and can either come equipped with twin laser beams, or explosive grenades.
t: Tachyon gunships are not very durable enemies, making up for the lack of thick armor with long-range attacks and hovering a medium distance away from Ratchet. As such, the Combuster and Fusion Grenade are effective against them early on, and later, and the Predator Launcher, Nano-Swarmers, and Negotiator are recommended for later engagements.

d: Dropships are a type of commonly recurring vehicle in the Ratchet & Clank series. They are used to transport soldiers and 'drop' them in the midst of battle against Ratchet and Clank. Some of them also had offensive capabilities, in which case they were often also deployed as gunships.

Talons are enemy ships in A Crack in Time. They are agorian dropships and star cruisers that battle Ratchet both in space and on land. They have animal-like bodies (with curved wings and large curved tails), and are capable both of firepower from a distance and of deploying agorians via teleportation.

Tank bots are enemies in Up Your Arsenal. Only two are encountered, one in the challenge "Meet Courtney - Gauntlet" (renamed to "BBQ Boulevard" on replays) on the Annihilation Nation, and one during the mission "Find Dr. Nefarious" alongside the tyhrranoids.

Technomite electro soldiers are enemies in Size Matters fought in the Technomite City on Challax. They are tall, bulky technomite infantrymen wielding a staff which, when slammed against the ground, creates a line of electricity that shocks anything passing through.

Technomite guard statues are enemies in Size Matters. They are stone automatons used by the technomites to defend the temple in the Vetega Jungle on Ryllus, in which the technomite map room was located. The statues stand about as tall as Clank and have a humanoid shape, wielding spiked clubs as weapons.

Technomite heavy troopers are enemies in Size Matters, encountered in the Medical Outpost Omega and on the Dayni Moon. They are technomite robot soldiers with a humanoid appearance and large, bulky yellow armor, which is in fact operated by a Robotic Control Unit.
Teratropes are enemies in A Crack in Time. They are large crab-like creatures that feed on quantum energy, allowing them to eat temporal recordings.
t: Teratropes are fought around the Great Clock as Clank and are often found alongside Breegus wasps. They are small enemies that are only capable of melee damage. They can be defeated in one hit by Clank's Chronoscepter, and a Time Bomb can slow them should they be a nuisance.

d: Tesladrones are enemies in Tools of Destruction and Before the Nexus. They are robotic attack drones utilized by the Imperial Army, which attack in melee range. Upon spotting an enemy, tesladrones activate their sirens as they chase their target on their unicycle.
t: Tesladrones are weak both in their armor and their attacks, and pose a minor threat even when found in numbers. Their attacks only come in melee range. Early on, the Fusion Grenade can destroy groups of them easily, and the Shock Ravager becomes particularly effective later.

d: Test dummies are enemies in Ratchet & Clank, the 2016 reimagined game, and Up Your Arsenal, with appearances in cutscenes in Going Commando. They are robots used by Gadgetron Corporation and Megacorp to test new products, including weapons.
t: Test dummies are generally slow-moving robots which attack with one of their Gadgetron weapons equipped, or the arm-mounted flamethrower. They are not usually durable and are simple in their movements, but their numbers can be overwhelming.

d: Thermosplitters are enemies in Tools of Destruction. They are small laser security bots that defend the Apogee Space Station. Ratchet and Clank fought them during "Search the Station".
Thrashers are enemies in A Crack in Time. They are medium-sized hovering robots that resemble small flying humanoid torsos with scythe blades for arms.

The three-eyed tyhrranoid was an enemy encountered in Up Your Arsenal. It is the primary shock troop of the tyhrranoids, often seen in groups to attack opponents or bar them from advancing. They have an orange-skinned stronger variant known as the three-eyed tyhrranoid V2. Once Dr.
t: The three-eyed tyhrranoid is more powerful than their one and two-eyed counterparts, but not as powerful as the four-eyed tyhrranoid or the ultra mecha-tyhrranoid. Since they attack in groups, it is best to maintain distance since as to not get hit by their attacks. Their recoil time also allows enough time for a quick dodge, before the last blasts aim for Ratchet.

d: }} Thug grenadiers are enemies in Into the Nexus. They are Thugs-4-Less mercenaries who attack by repeatedly throwing grenades that explode on contact.

}} Thugs-4-Less Brutes are enemies in Going Commando. They are Thugs-4-Less foot soldiers which carry a two handed-blaster that fires a burst of shots, and deploy Megacorp Chickenbots. Ratchet encountered them on the Maktar Resort, and later on the Prison Planet.
t: In Going Commando, standard Thugs-4-Less Brutes fire relatively slow missiles, which can easily be dodged. When coupled with Chickenbots swarming Ratchet, they can be a moderately greater threat. Though they are at their most dangerous when being warped in en masse by dropship.

d: Thugs-4-Less Carrier Ships are enemy vehicles piloted by the Thugs-4-Less in Going Commando, encountered on planet Gorn. They are large, grey warships with slow movement and several laser cannons.
Thrasher Cannon }} Thugs-4-Less Henchmen are enemies in Going Commando. They are Thugs-4-Less foot soldiers which carry a blaster, and often appear in groups of up to three.
t: The standard Thugs-4-Less Henchmen have relatively high durability and considerable firepower, and will whack Ratchet with their gun as a melee weapon if he comes too close. It is easy enough to predict the trajectory of the electric sphere fired from their blasters, making dodging or avoiding them altogether quite feasible.

d: Thugs-4-Less attack ships are enemies in Going Commando encountered in Canal City, Notak. They are Thugs-4-Less ships developed as successors to the Thug Flame Ship, and outfitted with a ranged flame attack, tinted windows, and a deluxe set of cup holders, in response to negative feedback.

Thugs-4-Less fighters are enemy vehicles piloted by the Thugs-4-Less in Going Commando. They are small fighter-craft that comprise part of the Thug fleet. They were encountered by Ratchet and Clank in the Star Explorer in the Wupash Nebula, the Feltzin System, and planet Gorn.
t: Green Thugs-4-Less fighters will fire at the Star Explorer by shooting in front of them, and often move in groups. Due to the volume of their attacks and their speed, they can deal heavy damage to the ship, in which case they should be evaded by boosting towards them and firing at them first, or by performing a barrel roll to dodge.

d: Thwogs are enemies in Tools of Destruction and background creatures in Rift Apart. They are three-eyed bat-like creatures that can be found in the Sarrdollow Caves of the pirate base on planet Ardolis, as well as on the docks. They are found usually in groups, and hang upside down from various ropes and wires.

Toxic crabs are enemies in Ratchet & Clank, the 2016 reimagined game, and Rift Apart. They are large crabs with giant claws and strong shells, often found amongst darters and woken by screamers. After taking a hit, they will immediately retaliate by striking with their claws.
t: ===Ratchet & Clank (2002)=== In the original release, when fought as Clank, toxic crabs remain stationary. Rather than attack these creatures himself, Clank should command Gadge-Bots to kill them.

d: }} Trash drones are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are drones flash-fabricated out of the scraps from previous experiments, with their radar being comprised mostly from old LEDs and their CPUs were wired together from old remote controls.

Tremors are enemies in Deadlocked. They are bipedal gladiator aliens fought in DreadZone. Ratchet fought them throughout his early time at DreadZone, first in the Marauder Tournament, and later on Kronos, and subsequently most other tournaments.
t: Tremors are dangerous due to their running speed and their quick melee attacks. Up to the Avenger Tournament they rely on melee attacks, and often appear in groups, making the Magma Cannon the most useful counter, alongside the B6-Obliterator with the Napalm Mod. The Holoshield Launcher is also effective in blocking them entirely.

d: Tumfoids are creatures in Tools of Destruction, mentioned in Into the Nexus. They are small, bipedal robots found in gelatonium plants that eat gelatonium. Tumfoids are not a traditional enemy, as they are entirely docile and do not attack Ratchet and Clank, nor can they be damaged.

The two-eyed tyhrranoid was a type of tyhrranoid encountered in Up Your Arsenal. They controlled all the tyhrranoid vehicles and machines, including Momma Tyhrranoid's backpack turret, possibly making them the most intelligent of the species.
t: The standard two-eyed tyhrranoid infantry is only encountered once and in a fairly large group, and is rather easily dispatched with either the Nitro Launcher or the Shock Blaster. At best, they can lay down fire peridiocally with their plasma pistols, but they lack both the speed and fire rate to make a serious threat besides their numbers.

d: }} Two-headed Smolgian snappers are enemies in Going Commando encountered in the Megacorp distribution facility on Smolg. They are creatures of average size, but with two heads extending from long necks, and a set of quadrupedal legs to support their armored body.
Tyhrranoids appear as enemies in Secret Agent Clank, fought by Ratchet as inmates of the Prison Planet.
t: Standard tyhrranoids have low toughness and deal little damage on their own, and their main strength is in numbers: if too many roll toward Ratchet at once, they can overwhelm him. The Dual Lacerators are quite effective, due to their ability to target multiple enemies at the same time. Other weapons acquired later with an area-of-effect are also helpful.

d: Tyhrranoid attack ships are enemies encountered in Up Your Arsenal. They are large red assault aircraft that were used during the tyhrranoids' ground offense on Veldin, with two being seen on Kyzil Plateau in "Save Veldin!", and another at the end of "Eliminate the Enemy Forces" in F-Sector.

Tyhrranoid dropships are a vehicle commonly used by the tyhrranoids in Up Your Arsenal. They were integral to the tyhrranoid invasions, and could be seen continuously flying around in the skies during the attacks. They were also seen in the skies of the Nefarious BFG area, Koros, and the command center, Mylon.
t: As per their name, dropships will often be seen dropping enemies off in the midst or at the start of a fight, reinforcing enemy positions. It is possible to destroy them with powerful weapons such as the Annihilator or Disc Blade Gun to preemptively take their occupants with them.

d: Ultra-Mech Unlimited units are massive robotic enemies in Ratchet & Clank encountered within the robot factory on planet Quartu.
t: The Ultra-Mech Unlimited units are exclusively engaged while playing as Giant Clank. Despite their intimidating size, they serve as minor obstacles; their rockets deal negligible damage, and their spiked ball attacks primarily serve to briefly interrupt the player's movement.

d: Undead goons, also known as bone goons, are enemies in Rift Apart. Hailing from a nightmare dimension, they are alternate counterparts to the Goons-4-Less. Undead goons comprise variants of the goon infantry, goon rusher, and zoom goons.

where: Scarstu Debris Field, Zurkie's (rusher and zoom)

t: Undead goons fight identically to their living counterparts, but are more durable, inflict more damager, and have increased ferocity. Undead goon rushers rise from the ground to attack opponents.

d: The undead pirates are enemies in Quest for Booty. They are space pirates on Merdegraw loyal to Captain Angstrom Darkwater, brought back from the dead due to the curse of Darkwater. Ratchet and Talwyn Apogee fought them on Merdegraw.
t: The buccaneer, hardy buccaneer, and corsair undead pirates are identical to their living counterparts in combat style, and capable of appearing from nowhere and fly in as green wisps or emerge from water, in addition to being deployed by pirate skiffs. The hot head pirates function as grenadiers, and Skull Walkers are akin to four-legged tanks with twin Gatling guns.

d: Undead sandsharks are enemies in Rift Apart. They are sandsharks from an alternate dimension where the living dead are common. Undead sandsharks presumably hail from the nightmare dimension that the undead goons are from.
Vroom goons are enemies in Rift Apart. They are heavy Goons-4-Less flying units fought invarious places. They use custom Megacorp hoverbikes,
t: Vroom goons are durable and mobile enemies. Their main attack is firing chained electric rods that fire across the ground toward Rivet, with chains of deadly electricity between them. Their electric rod attacks can be jumped over or avoided using a Phantom Dash; strafing is also a useful way to stay out of the way of their incoming trajectory, and the Void Repulser can be used to block them.

d: }} The waitresses are minor enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are humanoid feminine robots that serve at Le Paradis Des Tricheurs Casino.

Warbots are enemies in Ratchet & Clank (2016) and the movie. They are sentient, armored humanoid robots manufactured by Drek Industries for planetary invasions. Created by Dr. Nefarious and led by Victor Von Ion, these robots were built from high-grade raritanium at a factory in Skorg City on Quartu.
t: In battle, warbots can either engage from the ground or deploy their jetpacks to fire while hovering. They attack using ranged weapons, spreading their laser blasts to cover a wide area. These lasers deal substantial damage but travel slowly enough that they can be predicted and dodged with careful strafing. Due to their thick armor, warbots are highly resilient opponents.

d: }} Watchmen, or enforcement-bots, are enemies in Secret Agent Clank. They are security robots from planet Edificus.

Weevoids are enemies featured in All 4 One. These aggressive creatures are encountered throughout the N.E.S.T.. They have scorpion-like bodies with large pincers, a segmented tail, and a rock-like shell, along with a single eye and a tooth-filled maw.

Were-sheep, also known as angry rams, are enemies in Size Matters fought in the Farming Cooperative on Dayni Moon. They are sheep who change forms between day and night. During the daytime, they are peaceful, small sheep with a single leg for movement, and reside peacefully with the robot farmers.

Grungarian wrecking drones, often referred to as just wrecking drones, are robotic enemies in Full Frontal Assault. They are kamikaze robots belonging to the grungarian marauders that carry large explosives, which they use to destroy themselves and deal immense area-of-effect damage.
t: Wrecking drones are bipedal robots that serve as mobile bombs. They will rush towards a target—typically a player or a base generator—and slam their explosive payload down, resulting in a massive blast. As kamikaze units, they will also detonate upon being defeated, creating a large explosion that can be just as deadly.

d: Zoom goons are enemies in Rift Apart. A Goons-4-Less flying unit, they are equipped with jetpacks and remain airborne above the battlefield at all times, while using grenade launchers.
t: Zoom goons' jetpacks allow them to perform evasive aerial movements to dodge side to side and avoid your weapons attacks. Their method of attack is to lob grenades at their target, marked by a red reticle on the ground. Stay out of these to avoid getting hit, although the explosion from their grenades has a wide reach and even jumping over them when they detonate can still cause damage.

d: Zyphoids are enemies in A Crack in Time. These mushroom-like creatures emerge from spawners and appear in several varieties distinguished by size and coloration.
t: All zyphoid variants engage in close-quarters combat, utilizing headbutts (small) or bites (large). Large zyphoids can also lunge at targets, spit acid, or release toxic spore clouds that gradually drain the health of nearby enemies.
